utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Russo, I was informed that you would like to deal with a few matters prior to continuation of your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, very briefly. There is one unrelated matter with respect to the Helsinki Committee report, 65 ter 4674. We're simply seeking to get a MFI for that document so that is doesn't fall off the radar screen before the next MFI session. I understand there is are outstanding issues about redactions those are being taken care of. I just wanted to have it MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a MFI number for 65 ter 4674.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document shall be given Exhibit P2345, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Next, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Next, Mr. President, if we could briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The final thing, Mr. President, was -- I just wanted to alert the Chamber, on Friday I sent around a spreadsheet indicating all of the documents that I intend to tender from the bar table at the close of my examination. Those being the remainder of the attachments and annexes to the reports of Mr. Rajcic. I will be doing that at the conclusion. I didn't know if there was any issue with respect to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President, we have the issue that obviously it wasn't attached, but we also have the issue of what the preference of the Trial Chamber was with regard to artillery documents being tendered through a witness to allow that witness to explain them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo, of course, it's up to you to consider have these documents admitted through the witness, if there is no 65 ter issue left. Although there is a preference if you choose to tender it through the bar table then, of course, we would expect you to follow the guidance of the Chamber; that is, to give a brief description to draw your attention to any specific portions of the document, which are of primary interest and then to give this to the Defence first so that we have the usual procedure in place to considered a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, part of the reason I didn't do that to begin with is primarily these documents that -- the contextualisation that the Court sought preference for was -- I believe, is provided in the reports themselves to the extent that Mr. Rajcic cites to these annexes within the reports which have already been ordered into evidence, and by that, I believe he is demonstrating the relevance of those particular portions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But even then if in a table you set out -- see report, Mr. Rajcic, page so-and-so where he draws attention to this document then we know where to look. Otherwise we have to do all the -- all the research ourselves to reconstruct what -- what apparently was on the mind of the witness. So even if it follows from the report, then we'd like to know which part so the report, so that we can easily verify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will submit an amended spreadsheet, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The only issue with regard to the report is -- I mean the spreadsheet is not commentary on the probative value of this. If it is pointing the Chamber to a particular page in the report, that's fine but that -- we dont object to that per se other than our prior previously stated objections. What we do object to is any commentary going to the net worth of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think I earlier said that it has to be given to the Defence first, and if there is any disagreement on how neutral the reference could be, of course, Mr. Kehoe, to some extent drawing your attention to a certain portion, of course, has always some argumentative value or lack of value.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if would you please keep that in mind and if would you choose formulas which are as neutral as possible and mainly for purpose of drawing our attention to specific parties, so we don't have to find our way just by ourselves. Any other matter Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then one thing, there is a pending motion for protective measures, and if the Witness 13. Is my recollection right that we have not yet received the response.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We've drafted a response, and I know that, Your Honour, but I'm not certain whether it has been filed. But it will certainly be filed this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In view of our schedule, is there -- could all parties finally give their views on the matter this morning, either in writing or orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will take a look at it, Mr. President, but it would help if we knew exactly when Witness 13 is supposed to be coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry I have my witness numbers confused. I thought we had -- We'll check and get back to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. Mr. Russo, are you ready to continue your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could then, Mr. Usher, could you then escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Russo will now continue his examination-in-chief. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to get back to where we left off on Friday, and get some more information about you -- from you about General Gotovina's movements during the operation. I believe you've already indicated to us that General Gotovina was at his forward command post in Sajkovici when the attack began on the 4th of August; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know if he left Sajkovici at all during that day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you believe he travelled to on that date?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, he visited the Sibenik Operations Group as well as the Zadar one, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how exactly did he travel from one area to another on that day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he had an MI-8 helicopter at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And other than the areas that you have already mentioned, do you know if he went anywhere else on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did he return to Sajkovici towards the end of that day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did he hold any meetings in Sajkovici with the senior staff or anyone else concerning the operation on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did General Gotovina discuss with anyone on the evening of the 4th of August the decision to continue firing artillery at targets in Knin on the following morning?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know, why General Gotovina did decide to continue firing on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack continued. It is the ordinary combat activity, that artillery, as the form of combat support, be there at the disposal of infantry and other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was the army of the RSK or its leadership still in the town of Knin on 5 August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information available to me from the intelligence department, and based on electronic surveillance, we had information that they were still active in their coordination with the forces deployed along the front line, the first line of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand you had information that they were still active. What I'm attempting to discover is where, if you know, they were physically located, the RSK leadership.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that on the 5th, in the morning, they were still in the Slavko Rodic barracks and in the HQ of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like permission to show a non-65 ter document to the witness. This is one of the documents which had originally been submitted with the HV artillery bar table motion and at that is 65 ter 6130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Frankly, again, I don't know with what we're talking about. We are entitled to disclosure before this. We didn't get this disclosure that they put in there. It's not on the 65 ter list, and I don't know what methodology is being employed by the Prosecutor. We didn't get notice for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you first ask, Mr. Russo, when he received its, when he disclosed it, and what the reason is that it is not on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The document was received by us on the 12th of December of 2007, was disclosed to the Defence on the 28th of August, I believe, of -- I am sorry, it was received by us on 28th of August 2007. It was disclosed to the Defence on 12 December of 2007. We gave notice to the Defence that we intended to submit the document in the HV artillery bar table document motion. We sought to have it added to the 65 ter list. The Court denied that motion without prejudice and instructed us to bring in these documents with proper contextualisation with a witness on the stand. We did put it on the exhibit list for this witness, so I'm not certain where the argument that we did not give notice is arising from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The difference, of course, is between disclosure and whether or not they're going to use it. If it is a 65 ter document. There are literally I think that I needs to be clarified. There are literally thousand and thousand and thousands of documents that are disclosed, but as far as putting it on the 65 ter list and use and notice to the other parties, that is a completely different story. I take Mr. Russo at his word that it was, in fact, disclosed but again we have a situation where it is not on the 65 ter list and we were not properly informed that it was going to used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo says more. Mr. Russo says that he -- they tried to add it to the 65 ter list, that this was denied without prejudice and it is on the list of exhibits they wanted to use with this witness. That would not be true for thousands and thousands of documents would, it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was just -- I was looking -- using the terminology of disclosure when you disclose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm -- what I'm drawing your attention to is that I asked more than just about disclosure. I asked a few other matters as well. You have answered to the lack of disclosure -- to the -- to the possibility that it was among thousand witness thousands of disclosed documents whereas Mr. Russo said more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It was part of a series of documents that they wanted to put in their bar table -- bar table motion, that's right. That is, in fact, the case. I take Mr. Russo at his word for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And looking at my list here, it was, in fact, one of the documents that was a non-65 ter list that in one version of their exhibit list -- I believe it's the last one they intended to try to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, the Chamber's ruling is that you're allowed to show it to the witness, which is not a decision yet on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could please have 65 ter 6130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I add to that, Mr. Kehoe that if the Defence would need more time because of certain -- certainly flaws in announcing the use in whatever way, that the Chamber invites you to inform the Chamber about it so that we can consider that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could go to the bottom of the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I will begin reading at the last sentence on page 1 in English. I believe that this entire portion is on page 2 of the B/C/S, the portion that I'm going to be reading. Now, Mr. Rajcic, this is an analysis by the commander of the 4th Guards Brigade, and he indicates: "By the start of Oluja 95, Knin was, in fact, in a hopeless situation, and condemned to wait for the final blow ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could move to the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: He continues: "Turning to Operation Oluja 95 itself, it needs to be said that the enemy's front defence was the slopes -- the front defence line was the slopes of the Knin Pljesevica mountain, breached by bringing in of the 4th Guards Brigade, and the liberation of Knin was thus at hand. "The use of an encircling manoeuvre and the capture of the dominant features in the vicinity of the town of Knin meant that street fighting was avoided, because the so-called RSK army and the population evacuated on the night of day one." Now, Mr. Rajcic, do you agree with the assessment of commander of the 4th Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, is this the reference -- is there a reference date on there? I'm sorry. Is that the 14th of August, is that the document we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think we will have to turn to the first page to see the date of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the 14th of August. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you agree with the commander's assessment in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with this. I've never seen this analysis before. This is the analysis of the commander of the 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you don't agree with it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can the question be more previous, please. What exactly you refer to. I have never seen the analysis before. The 4th Guards Brigade launched attacks on the second day of Operation Storm, not on the first day. I do know for a fact that it was on Pljesevica, that it was engaged in fighting in the village of Golubic [Realtime transcript read in error, "Golugica"], which is on the outskirts of the town of Knin on that day. As far as I remember, it was on the 5th of August, throughout the day and in the early evening. That's something that I can talk about now. As for this entire document, that's all I can tell you at this point, ad hoc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just with respect to page 12, line 9, I believe the witness identified a different village which I don't think will be disputed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rajcic, you said, "I know for a fact that it was on Pljesevica that it was engaged in fighting in the village of," and what did you then say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Village of Golubic, which is ahead of the town of Knin on the way to the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were just seeking to have the right name on the record because it was transcribed by another name. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, what I'm seeking to determine is whether or not you agree with the commander's assessment that street fighting was avoided in Knin because the so-called RSK army had fled on the night of day one.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would offer into evidence 65 ter 6130.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same objection as previously stated, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The document will be marked for identification. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit P2346, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo, there are quite a number of documents attached to this one. It's a 11-page document all together. Do we need all the other documents which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We only need to the portion of the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first two pages, therefore. Could you then please take care that the document, in the way you want to tender it, will be uploaded, and give notice to Mr. Registrar once you have uploaded under the same number, the two-page document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would now seek permission to show to the witness another document which is procedurally in the same posture as the previously document. It was on the HV bar table document motion, also on the exhibit list, but is not on the 65 ter list, and this is 65 ter 6142.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I take it that the same objections would apply here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Same ruling applies as well. You're allowed to put it to the witness, Mr. Russo, which is not a decision on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could please have 65 ter 6142.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you can see this is Croatian intelligence report dated 4 August 1995. It appears that the report was sent at 2130 hours, and first I'd like to ask you something with respect to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move down in the English version a bit, to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now there are numbers which appear above each of the paragraphs and I wanted to ask but those. Do you see -- well, let's just take the first paragraph that begins: "A member who is reporting from the village of Tenje." Above that are numbers 069520408952019A. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now there are similar entries for each paragraph in this document. I wanted to confirm with you what those numbers stand for. There is the first numbers in the series, that is 06952 appears to be some form of serial number. But the numbers that follow, are the same for each entry and that is 040895. And I'd like to know whether that indicates the date of the communication, the 4th of August, 1995. And the numbers that follow; for example, 2019A, refers to 2019 hours, during the day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move to the second page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S, Mr. Rajcic, I'm interested in the third paragraph from the bottom, and in the English version, I believe -- well, the entry below where it says GS SVK and that indicates: "The Knin leadership abandoned the city and went in the direction of Drvar, through Srb. They turned left when they left the place, then 30 kilometres later, right." Do you recall seeing this intelligence report, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Gotovina was receiving intelligence reports on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, you don't know if he was receiving reports; or, no, he didn't receive reports?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was receiving them. We were not on the same premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would offer 65 ter 6142.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same objections, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please assign a number so that the document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P2347, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, how many RSK army troops, combat troop, did you believe were in the town of Knin on 5 August, in the town of Knin proper?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An estimation can be very relative. The army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina had mobilised all men, aged between 18 and 65, and this is a situation that prevailed through to the end of the war. I believe that everything that was able-bodied and able to carry a weapon was at their disposal. What sort of numbers those were, I wouldn't like to speculate on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that, and I do understand there was a mobilisation of conscripts or everyone for the RSK army. However, that's a different matter from the deployment. Do you know -- and if you don't, that's fine. I just want to know if you have idea of the combat troops were deployed inside the city?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the number for the town proper. But they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how about on the first day of the attack, the 4th of August? Do you have any estimation of how many were in the town on that day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to make an analysis based on the information available to me, it was the Dinara combat group, which had the strength of 1.000 to perhaps 1.500 troops. There were several HQs in Knin with all the attendant troops, establishment-wise and logistics-wise from the level of the Main Staff of the SVK, the command of the 7th Corps, the command of the mixed artillery regiment, the support artillery regiment, the command of the light- and high-aircraft regiment, with the necessary protection personnel, in order to secure all the important facilities in Knin and insignificant for the military, and such facilities that were of importance for the SVK in Knin can be identified. In fact, I had a document from their assistant for anti-aircraft defence, where he organised and deployed anti-aircraft defence units. There was the police of Mile Martic, in the monastery of St. Ante in Knin. Some of their units were stationed Knin or Mindzusari earring wearers or something of the sort. In the Senjak barracks, they had the command of the already mentioned artillery regiment complete with the logistics troops; and in the Slavko Rodic barracks, they had their operational reserve forces for possible interventions along the lines of defence that were threatened the most. They were there if need be. And I do recall there was an insignificant unit, insignificant in terms of what was of interest to us, in the new school in Knin. If we were to take all of this into consideration, according to their establishment and their strength, and make a head count of all of them; and, of course, we would have to see to what extent they were manned, whether they were fully manned, only then would I be able to give you an answer. Excuse me, in Golubic --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a camp for --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I was asking specifically about the town of Knin. I don't want to expand it beyond that. Now have you named a number of HQs and a number of different kinds of units. Can you tell us where we can find this information in HV documentation. What documents can we look at to see that you had information specific about the numbers of troops in any of these places or that there were troops present in these places on the 4th of August? Where can we find that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea where you'd be able to find that. Logically speaking, there was intelligence and security work carried out. They dealt with such information, as well as some other services. They were looking into where their troops were. I believe one could find all that in the archives of the Ministry of Defence. At least it should be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was your information about the number of civilians inside of the town of Knin on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information we had was official. As I have mentioned in the past few days, the information was that already in June, civilians began leaving Knin, when the Croatian forces reached the dominant features of Mount Dinara. Going by the semi-official information I had received from the people on the other side - that is to say, Serbs - who -- whom I knew before the war because they were from the area that I hailed from, they were saying that people began moving out as early as that time. According to the information I had, going by the census of 1990, the town or settlement of Knin, as an administrative unit, had some 12.300 inhabitants, out of which some 1600 Croats; basically all of them had been expelled by various means and in various ways. There were some 800 inhabitants of other ethnic backgrounds. If I try to do my math, at the beginning of the conflict, it means that there must have been some 10.000 inhabitants. If we take into account all of those who were between the age of 18 and 60, who were mobilised, all able-bodied men, and if we take into account that prior to Operation Storm, a number of people were expelled or left of their own accord for various reasons, then the figure would be such as the one I said. According to the information that I had prior to Operation Storm, in the area of the settlement of Knin which, covers the area of six square kilometres, there may have been between 2 and 3.000 civilians. According to the 1990 census, the settlement of Knin had some 3600 households. Based on all that, I conclude that there was a small number of civilians in that six square kilometres area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you have any information that civilians from the areas of Grahovo and Glamoc and Strmica were going to the area of Knin, prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them -- or at least not all of them. I don't know how many exactly. Some left towards Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, where was General Gotovina on the 5th of August, when the artillery attack resumed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 5th of August, or at least as regards the 5th of August, I can tell you that I saw General Gotovina early in the morning, because, on the 4th of August, during the night, or perhaps on the 5th of August in the morning, we spent together in a nearby house. We slept there for a couple of hours. The next day, just prior to the beginning of combat on the 5th of August, I was at my duty station in the operations centre. As of that point of time, until early evening I had no contact with General Gotovina, save for one occasion when he called me into his office early in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Gotovina went to Knin after Croatian troops entered the town on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know if General Gotovina was aware of what the troops were doing in Knin after they entered the town?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he knew. I had information that the assistant commander for security, Mr. Pavic, went there. He told me that he went there on orders of General Gotovina. He had been at the operations centre. He was supposed to go to Knin to attend to some of his tasks. I have information that General Ademi went to Knin that day as well. I don't know to do what, but as he was leaving the operations centre, he said that he was going to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know, what Croatian troops were doing after they entered the town of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't think about it after I had received information that the settlement of Knin was no longer of any artillery interest. If I try to think about what the soldiers were doing, according to the tasks, they were supposed to conduct a manoeuvre around Knin; and, at that time, that was enough information for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you have any information that Croatian soldiers started drinking and looting in the town on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Gotovina received any information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to show the witness a document which is not on the 65 ter list. It is an attachment to his report, which is now P2339. It is 65 ter 7069.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the provisional 65 ter number, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, may I take it that the same objection applies --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to all attachments to the reports because we have different categories now by now, I think, those who were attachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add it to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if could I have please have 65 ter 7069.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you attached this as attachment number 3 to the first reconstruction that you did. It is the 7th Guards Brigade operations diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move to B/C/S page 2, English page 3. You can see there at the entry for 1100 hours, it indicates that the unit entered Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we move to the next page, please, in the English, and also the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We can see at the entry for 1155 hours it indicates that word was sent that the military police be sent to Knin and that the military police were sent. Now, do you know why word was sent that the military police should go to Knin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, this is something that does not come as a surprise. It's standard operative work that the military police follows up in sequence after the troops. I don't know what the background of this situation was though.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page in the English but stay on the same page in B/C/S just move a little bit down in the B/C/S version, to the entry for 2007 hours --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It indicates that Brigadier Ademi, who I believe you indicated was on his way to Knin, issues an order to secure HTV Croatian television Knin from plunder or devastation. Now do you know why Brigadier Ademi needed to issue an order to protect Croatian television from plunder or devastation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would move for the admission of 65 ter 7069.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you mark it for identification. Mr. Kehoe, same objections apply, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit P2348, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Again, Mr. Kehoe, here also applies that if the non-appearances on the 65 ter list would require further time for preparation, the Chamber would like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, can you tell us if General Gotovina held any meetings with the senior staff members of the Split Military District during or after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have in mind the command of the Croatian forces, within the Military District of Split and the Croatian Defence Council, such meetings were held on a regular basis in terms of briefings in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now when you say "regular basis," can you tell us how often. Was it every day, every other day, once a week?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a rule in place at the time, unless ordered otherwise, stating that each evening, in the evening hours, there was to be a briefing session with the commander, attended by the commanders and chiefs from the Military District command. When I say "chiefs," I mean the chiefs of branches, as well as professional services.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were representatives of the military police present at these briefings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, it was seldom. They were under no obligation to attend such briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were representatives of the information and security service, that is SIS, ever at attendance at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were there officers of the information and security service amongst HV combat units during the operation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did they provide information, both to their own headquarters as well as to General Gotovina, regarding the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to show the witness a document. It is not on the 65 ter list, and it is not an attachment to any of his reports. It is 65 ter 7122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, you certainly remember that I asked some questions last time about the documents you wanted to show. If you would spontaneously give that information, then the Chamber would not have to ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The document was seized by the Prosecution on 14 July 2008, was disclosed to the Defence on the 19th of September, 2008. The original was disclosed on 19th September, and the translation was disclosed only recently, on the 10th of February of 2009.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any explanation for the period between the 19th of September and 10th of February?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What kind of document is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It's a report from one of the information and security service agents who were placed among a HV combat unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, leave is granted to show it to the witness, which is not a decision on admission. Mr. Kehoe, especially in view of the fact that the translation was disclosed only recently, if there's any more time needed, whereas the original -- and I see it was only disclosed and not announced as an exhibit to be used in September. If you would need additional time, you may inform the Chamber and ask for a relevant remedy. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have 65 ter 7122.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, you can see this is a report, a summary report by a SIS officer who was placed in the Operational Group Sibenik, and I would like to focus on item 5, which appears on English page 4, B/C/S page 3. Looking at the second-to-last sentence in item 5 it states: "Once the operation was finished, a decrease of discipline was noted amongst quite a number of HV members which led to" --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a short while I wasn't able to see the whole page. If you zoom in, then I have portions of the text missing. Now that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will begin again: "Once the operation was finished a decrease of discipline was noted amongst quite a number of HV members which led to alcohol consumption and looting of houses in liberated places. "When the operation was finalised, the HV members slightly lost their composure due to the exhaustion and exhilaration with the success."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move now to item number 8, which appears at English page 5, and B/C/S page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And there it indicates: "The conduct of HV members while entering inhabited settlements was correct. However, once the settlements were occupied (particularly places inhabited)" --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you need item 8 focussed on any more, or is this enough for you to see?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I will begin again: "The conduct of the HV members while entering inhabited settlements was correct. However, once the settlements were occupied (particularly places inhabited by Serbs), the commanders lost a control over their soldiers which resulted in a number of torched houses and cases of robbery, particularly in the area of Djevrska, Kistanje, and Drnis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I see that we have two items 8, isn't it? That is a bit confusing. You were reading from the second item 8 and not from the first one. Is that -- because the -- both are now presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, I see that in B/C/S there's two item 8's although it looks like in the English there is item 8 and item 9. I was reading from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can't see that because then I would have to look at a previous page, if there's 8 and 9 then you would expect 9 to be the second section 8 in the original, but that is not the case because what you were reading is the second paragraph 8, which certainly does not correspond with item 9 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, from the B/C/S original, Mr. President, I am looking at the second item 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the second item 8 in B/C/S is the first item 8 in the English. So then we would have to look back and see -- 7 corresponds with the -- the 7 in the original corresponds with the English translation, and it looks as if the first item 8 in the original is not part of the translation, and that we continue. So, therefore, we have an incomplete -- apparently incomplete translation, if my analysis is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think, actually, Mr. President, if you look at the item 9 in the English version it appears to correspond to the first item 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That looks -- because there's a reference to the Operational Group Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the only thing I established until now that there was a reference to Operation Group Sibenik but then, of course, the next thing we have to do to look at the original and see -- Could we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, if you read the first lines in the original, paragraph 8 you see that the -- the first lines of the first item 8, then you see that although the Operational Group Sibenik is referred to that all the other things we find in the translation does not appear in the original. I see no General Staff; I see no reference to the -- in the original I see no reference to the 306 Detachment to the LOB Sibenik. So your explanation quick but not reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could perhaps, Mr. President, for a quick-fix we will, of course, have a revised translation uploaded, but for completeness we could ask the witness to simply read the first item 8 in the original B/C/S, have a translation on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't know what it actually says, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then please try to find out what it says before we spend time on witnesses to read portions of a document where you are apparently curious to know what is in there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can just tell you briefly, and I will make a representation to Mr. Russo, that it deals with the seizure of ARSK documents; and the fact that they're analysing these documents which have been recovered in the area. I don't think it is relevant to the examination of this witness. But I wanted to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, you will have to satisfy yourself with that for the time being. Thank you Mr. Misetic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and my thanks to counsel. If we could move in the B/C/S version to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And continuing on at the top it indicates: "We did not note any case of a war crime committed by an HV member. "In spite military and police operated check-points and the order on its function, it has been noted that a large quantities of technical equipment were taken from the liberated settlements." Now, Mr. Rajcic, to your knowledge was General Gotovina aware of the kind of conduct that is being reported by this SIS officer?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer your question, can I please have page 1 to see the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Page 1 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the date is 11th of August, but let's check at the beginning of the document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I saw this document for the first time when I was working for the government of the Republic of Croatia, because it bears the reference number S-44, which means that I set it apart from all the other documents that I had at my disposal. This is the period after the end of Operation Storm. In this particular area -- or, rather, I was present personally in that area between the 5th and the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you see Croatian soldiers consuming alcohol, looting houses, and torching houses in that area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you disagree that this was actually happening?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the dates, I can't state anything with any certainty, after the 7th or 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now you didn't answer my question about whether or not you were aware of -- whether or not General Gotovina either received this report or received the information contained in this report during his briefings.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that he could have received it on the 11th, at the earliest.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that officers of -- or representatives of the information and security service were present during the briefings for General Gotovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not representatives. A representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do you know whether that representative passed along information such as this to General Gotovina at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the 11th of August, I can say that he did not pass it on, not to General Gotovina but to me, because I was in charge of the briefings between the 8th and the 11th of August at the IZM, Sajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Briefings, which occurred on the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th, was General Gotovina present for those briefings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the 5th of August. I don't know about the 6th, because I was in the Skradin-Kistanje-Padjene area. For the 8th of August, I don't think he was. I was in charge of that regular evening briefing. I think that he dropped by for a brief moment on the 9th at some point during the briefing. After that particular briefing, he issued me a task. Since the Knin was to become the garrison of the Military District, I was supposed to remain at the Sajkovici IZM and see to it that the forward command post was disbanded and technically dismantled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could check the word that the witness used at page 31, line 24, the sixth word there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The abbreviation, which P is an abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, the line above that abbreviation, there's a word directly above that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rajcic -- there's a difference in line numbers on the one screen compared to the other. You said, "since Knin was become to the" -- what then? To become what of the Military District?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That a command post be set up in Knin, because under the establishment it was the forward command post at the time since the command post was in Split.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, you indicated earlier that in the evening of the 5th of August, General Gotovina called you to his office and tasked you with something. Can you tell us what that was about?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his office, General Gotovina had an operational working map onto which he plotted the way combat unfolded across the area of the Split Military District. Along the axis of the Sibenik Operations Group that is to say, Bribirski-Mostinje-Skradin axis, Djevrska-Kistanje axis the pace of attack was not satisfactory. In other words -- Your Honour, can we move no closed session, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you in private session. That is there is no communication. Otherwise we have to get all the curtains down. I don't think that would be necessary, would it? Just the words spoken to be -- Yes, we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you now say will not be related to the outside world. Please proceed, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically the 15th Home Guard Regiment did not make significant advances in the attack. At around 1800 hours on the 5th of August, General Gotovina summoned me to his office. He even made a joke by saying, These -- that lot of yours did not even liberate your own home at the time, and he said it as if appearing to be issuing me with an order. He told me, Take whatever you need and carry out a manoeuvre with all the assets you need in that area. The order is as follows: To reach the area of Padjene as soon as possible by skirting the inhabited settlements, by steering away from them. The task has to be accomplished before night-fall. The 4th Guards Brigade had already gone passed the Krka and is in the area of Tangina Glava, the village of Oceslovo. That lot down there is not doing anything. I asked that we move into closed session out of deference towards my comrades-in-arms. They should have some gratification for taking part in the fighting which led to the liberation of the Republic of Croatia or of its occupied areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I inquire with the parties whether the reason given by the witness to ask to move into private session would be a sufficient one under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We have no objection, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand that. I would have to take a look at the Rules specifically. Can I do that at the break, but at this juncture there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may add something. If it is going to be an issue for the Chamber I think there should be an inquiry as well about a Rule 75, if I can phrase it that way for him, just in the abundance of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Our position, Mr. President, is that this is not a proper basis for remaining in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For being --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: For being in private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rajcic, the Chamber will further consider whether the reason you gave for turning into private session is, from point of view of law of procedure, a solid reason. Of course, we didn't know what you were about to say. We'll consider that. Is there anything you would like to add, why in relation to the reason why you wanted to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I came to the HQ at night, I came across -- or, rather, I found the officers at the command post, at the HQ, sleeping. They were not in full combat readiness. That's why I asked for it. I simply want to be -- to treat them correctly. That's why I asked that we move into private session. I don't think it's necessary for these details to reach the public. I know that journalists, for various reasons known to them, are always waiting there to get hold of piquant pieces of news.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I did understand. You did not want to expose your former colleagues to any criticism where they have no opportunity to avail themselves to give any response what you're -- well, let's say blame them for, more or less. I asked you, because the Chamber would not, without proper reasons, and not by surprise, would make public where you initially asked it not to be made public. Nevertheless, the Chamber will consider the matter and for this reason wanted to know exactly the reasons why you wanted to go into private session. We move in open session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would move for the admission of 65 ter 7122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document should be MFI'd. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, similar objections, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Similar objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be given Exhibit P2349, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at the clock, Mr. President, it appears time for a break. I don't know ... I have a bit more of my examination left. I told the Chamber I would only have one session, but I do have about 30 minutes more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider during the break. I would, however, have one question to you, Mr. Rajcic, before we have a break. In this report that was read to you, we read that - this was the intelligence report, this item 8 - we read that the conduct of the HV members while entering inhabited settlements was correct but that once the settlements were occupied, particularly places inhabited by Serbs, that the commanders lost control -- or it says a control which is not entirely clear to me, over their soldiers which resulted in a number of torched houses and cases of robbery, and then some specific places are mentioned. The next line then reads: "We did not note any case of war crime committed by an HV member." Could you explain to us how the first portion of this item 8 and the line I just read, how to reconcile them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, between the 5th and 6th of August, and on the 6th of August while I was there, there was no torching or looting going on. There was a degree of relaxation among the troops. The information about Knin having been liberated was already widely known and had already been reported through the media. While I was there, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- along the ways where I travelled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. You, several time, relied in your answers on intelligence information. At this moment, I'm asking you to focus on what is written in this intelligence report and to explain to us, not on the basis of your own information, how to reconcile these several parts of item 8 because I understood from your answers that you have some experience in -- in interpreting intelligence information. So I'm asking you to focus -- if you need it on your screen, it is still there, although the second line is on the next page. But what is described there at the conclusion that, "We did not note any case of a war crime committed by an HV member." That is what I'd like to hear your comment on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only explanation I can give is that this text does not only encompass the 11th of August but several days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I was not mainly focussing on how many days but on how to -- on the one hand side, to say commanders lost control over their soldiers; result: number of torched houses; cases of robbery. And then: "We did not note any case of a war crime committed."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot explain such contextual matters unless I go into very lengthy elaborations. That is my subjective view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that gives us an explanation, then I would like to hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The period leading to the forces reaching Padjene did not have -- have any events. The civilian authority was established. The period between the 8th and the 11th of August might have been marked by some dishonest deeds having been committed, if any indeed. Who the culprits were, I can't tell you. I can't pinpoint them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a break, Mr. Rajcic, and we resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo you have another 20 minutes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, over the weekend, did you have any contact with any member or former member of the Croatian armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Over the weekend, did you have any contact with any member of the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with anyone with respect to the testimony that you've given here or that you will be giving, and I don't mean just speaking to them. I mean either by e-mail or any other form of communication.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going back to the briefings that General Gotovina had, can you tell us whether or not there were any representatives of the political affairs department at any of these briefings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Knin? And during what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Beginning on the 4th of August and from that date forward, through August and/or September.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in Knin on any briefings. On the 11th of August, I disbanded a command post at Sajkovici, or perhaps it was on the 12th, the forward command post, that is. And that is when I started working at the forward command post in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think you might be missing the focus of my question, Mr. Rajcic. I'm not limiting the location of where these meetings may have occurred. I just want to know if General Gotovina had briefings, wherever they may have occurred, between the 4th and August, and afterwards, if he had meetings at which members of the political affairs department were present.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were standard daily briefings, and it was a normal thing to have the Deputy Commander in charge of political affairs to attend such meetings or briefings, as you call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned that you were heading meetings between -- I believe you said the 8th and 11th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us why General Gotovina was not heading up those meetings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me he needed to be elsewhere, not in the area, and that I should take over the information evening meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you have any information on where he was during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Gotovina went on his honeymoon any time between the 8th and the 15th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that later, that piece of information. However, while I was in charge of the briefings, I did not have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And who was in charge of the responsibilities of the command of the Split Military District in General Gotovina's absence?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the forward command post that had been established in Knin, I think it was supposed to be General Ademi or General Rakic who were in charge. In terms of subordination, they were the next senior officers following General Gotovina. I remained in Sajkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And for this period of General Gotovina's absence, do you know or have any information as to whether or not he continued to be informed of events occurring within the Split Military District during that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. When he dropped by once, I did share some information with him, as regards the area that I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was there any discussion with General Gotovina or amongst any of his senior officers that he should not leave the area at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I only implemented the orders I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, were you present at a meeting on the 6th of August, a meeting with General Gotovina which took place in the Knin fortress?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Have you ever seen the video of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw that video?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was broadcast on the Croatian national television. It's channel 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And you're aware of some of the matters that General Gotovina is -- or was complaining about during that meeting; in particular, the behaviour of the troops in the town; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood the gist of General Gotovina's criticism levelled at his subordinate officers. Mr. Russo, I even have my own DVD copy of that meeting. I have it at home. Or a CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And you're aware, then, that he refers to the conduct of his troops as he likens them to barbarians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do you know what he based that assessment on?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably based it on the improper behaviour or conduct he had heard of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do you know what, if anything, General Gotovina did about that improper conduct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and I have already partially answered that question when you asked me what sort of a person General Gotovina was, he was a strict person. He undertook a series -- or issued a series of orders. He also initiated a number of disciplinary proceedings, in keeping with the rules of service of the armed forces, and he had the provisions of those rules at his disposal. He had the authority to initiate a disciplinary procedure and issue disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, as an officer of the Croatian armed forces, if you see or saw a HV member either looting a house, setting it on fire, or committing any kind of a crime, what exactly is it that you do about it, at that moment you observe it happening?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we shouldn't talk in the conditional or about hypothesis. I actually did something. On the 6th of August in Kistanje, I saw a single soldier attempting to take something from a house. I ordered him to leave it. I took him out of the combat establishment and sent him back to his home command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now if -- I understand that that is what you actually did on an occasion. But if there are a large number of soldiers engaging in this type of conduct and they are refusing orders to stop doing it, how do you handle that as an officer?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the armed forces, or, rather, in the MOD, we have our own bodies in charge of that, to impose measures. Should I clarify perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe there was a word that was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is page 43, line 10, he used an adjective to describe the first word there, which was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic you said: "In the armed forces, or, rather in the MOD, we have our own bodies in charge of that, to impose measures." This is not apparently a complete translation of what you said. Could you add what was now left out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when talking about the Ministry of Defence, I meant to say that at the level of the ministry, there was the military police as per establishment. Inside the armed forces, there are standard operative procedures when commanders can use the - so to speak - healthy part of their troops, to use them in order to prevent the recalcitrant or unsoldierly portion of his troops in order for those to cease with such behaviour, if we are talking about such periods as when there is combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, we saw earlier in the operations diary of the 7th Guards Brigade that the military police was sent to Knin about an hour after the 7th Guards Brigade itself entered the town. You indicated that this was quite normal procedure during these combat operations. Now, if General Gotovina disapproves of what those troops are doing on the 6th of August in the town and the military police are in the town, can he tell those military police to arrest the people committing crimes?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can use their line of command for it to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When you say "their line of command," I want to be clear about this. If there are military police in the town with him, and soldiers are also in that town committing those crime, can he tell those military police officers himself to arrest the individuals committing those crimes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the form of the question: Can he tell. I think he needs to be more specific in terms of exactly what is he asking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think the question is quite clear, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Formally speaking, he can try to do that, but he had no command authority over the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If he had no command authority over the military police, then how could he try to do that, formally speaking? I'm not sure I understand what you mean by formally speaking he can try to do that. How exactly would he do it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I refer to the formal part, it means that a general, in an armed force, can tell a soldier who is not under his command in terms of establishment to do something, but this does not entail the concept of executive command. In this case, it will be General Gotovina. If we are talking about the military police as needed, in his combat area, he can submit a request to the military police administration, or to the unit which, operationally speaking, is in the general area of combat, if so regulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, I do believe I understand the situation which you're speaking in the second part. However, I wanted to focus on the first part of your question [sic] and be clear about it. I mean, correct me if I'm wrong, but if General Gotovina witnesses his own troops looting and burning houses is he not going to place a phone call to Zagreb or send a letter to Zagreb asking them to tell the military police soldier next to him to do something about it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- yes. First of all, I notice that we have now two Gotovina Defence counsel intervening in the -- not only in matters of formulation but also on the substance of the way in which questions are phrased. That's unusual. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were -- the frequency point of view, you seem to be the one who deals with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it's the form. It's the form of the question. If he wants to ask a straight question, it's fine and he is obviously giving a scenario that has no applicability here. If he is going ask a particular question consistent what he is asking. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to join in the objection. It is more of a closing argument than it is of a question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your question is saying what Mr. Gotovina would not do in order to find out what the witness knows he should have done is not the way in which this should it be put to the witness. Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just apologise. The reason that I rose is, as the Court will know from a year of us in the courtroom, Mr. Kehoe has one set of issues that he deals. I deal with the other, and Mr. Russo had now crossed into my area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I thought, as a matter of fact, and, therefore, I think it was rather moderate in just saying that I observed, nothing else so that I now that I'm aware of these kind of procedural matters. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I find by the way -- I find a bit of an imprecision in what one observed in a command position. That could mean a lot of things. Personally see something to happen, to observing that this is reported to you, I don't know what you had on your mind or did you include in your question that where you asked how Mr. Gotovina would -- would respond that he would have personally observed everything or whether it came to his knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I was making reference to the fact that he had knowledge of it occurring in a particular place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why not ask Mr. Rajcic directly. Mr. Rajcic, if Mr. Gotovina would have had a -- I call him Mr. Gotovina because not out of any disrespect for the rank he had, but he appears here as an individual. If Mr. Gotovina would have had knowledge of a -- not a sporadic but a frequent occurrence of behaviour which was unacceptable, in terms of engaging the military police in any investigation, what would he have to do? Just request to the chief of military police, is that -- Mr. Russo, what you wanted to know, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is actually a part of what I wanted know, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have the first part. And then you ask the second part later. What, in your view, what action should he have taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He could ask of the military police battalion commander to initiate a procedure based on the provisions of the rules of discipline. Then they could submit a report, and in consultation with the legal department, a disciplinary measure or other measure can be imposed, as is envisaged by the Law on Defence Forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, second part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or still on the same part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: In reference to the situation on the 6th of August for which you have indicated you've seen the video where General Gotovina is referencing the behaviour of the troops in the town on that date, in that situation where he is present at the location where these crimes are being committed, and if members of the military police are also present along with him, at that particular location, what happens in that situation? How should he act in that situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, are we talking as a result of this meeting or during this meeting? I am a little bit confused, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Location, is that a reference to where they were all together televised.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, I mean in Knin. The meeting is occurring in Knin, and if I'm not mistaken General Gotovina is making reference to the conduct of his troops occurring in Knin at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
