utterances.text: And I think we should just go to the tape of exactly what General Gotovina tells the military police. It is in evidence as to what he says. It doesn't need have an opinion from someone who wasn't even there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think, given the witness's position, he is in a position to tell us what an HV officer would do or should do in a similar situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the question then is whether he did what he should have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: First, I think we need to establish what he should have done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether you start on the one side or on the other is ... What you followed the -- the exchange of thoughts. On the 6th, military police, Mr. Gotovina, both being present in Knin, what do you consider he should have done, if he had knowledge of non-sporadic disorderly behaviour of the kind we discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What he should have done is within the framework of the powers that were vested in him as commander, he was to have pronounced punitive measures or measures for misdemeanour through the military police if any such actions were committed, and he was to demand that soldiers of different levels were put in to custody. And then in according with rules through his legal service, he should have and did, in fact, pronounce many measures for breaches of discipline, including, for instance demobilisation, putting away from units demoting and let me not enumerate all the numerous instances of breaches of discipline of which there were over a thousand for the duration of this period. If this is a satisfactory answer. Because I did say at the beginning that these were to have been the procedures, and the question was asked in the conditional mode to the effect of what would have happened if something else had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have no further questions Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo. Mr. Kehoe, you will be the first to cross-examine Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President. My apologies, I didn't formally move across the bar table, the documents. I know the Court wants me to submit a new spreadsheet to do that. I will do that, however, I just want it to be clear that that spreadsheet is formal or will be formal motion to admit those documents across the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One it is finalised and once the Defence has had a look at it, we'll further consider the matter. Mr. Rajcic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe, who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President we will proceed with cross-examination. I note that Your Honour said if we needed additional time to review documents that counsel has given late notice, the OTP has given late notice, obviously that is difficult to do under certain time constraints. Nevertheless, we will attempt to do so as best we can but, of course, we reserve that position given the time constraints that we have before us. If I may, Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher, if I could give a hard copy of the witness's statement to him in his own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I proceed Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, good morning, sir. Mr. Rajcic, you recall meeting myself and other members of the Gotovina Defence team in Split on the 7th, 9th, 11th, 12th, and 13th of February, 2009; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too. I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Rajcic, do you recall signing a statement on the 13th of February, 2009?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if we could bring up on the screen 1D00-0767.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, what we're going to bring up on the screen is a copy of your statement in Croatian that was signed -- that you will take a look at. It should be -- it is a duplicate of what you have before you as well as the English version. Mr. Rajcic, you are free to look at the screen on the document that is before you, but quite simply, did you have a chance to review this statement before you began to testify before this Chamber last week?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you -- in reviewing this statement, does this statement accurately reflect what you told to members of the Gotovina Defence team during the aforementioned dates in February?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except for a typo in item 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us about that, typo in item 6? I don't know if it's important or not. Can you tell about that typo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2 of this document, Mr. Usher. It should be item 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going to item 6, Mr. Rajcic, could you please tell us what that typo is.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a wrong word. Is says -- it says the commander areas, but what it should actually read is the Military District Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So that would be in the -- it does in fact say the Split Military District in English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can just fix the Croatian consistent with what you just noted for us. Moving on to the next question. Was the statement that you provided to the General Gotovina Defence team true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was the statement that you provided and that's contained in that statement, was it true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to review it in total, because I signed every single sheet. I mean, this copy that have I before me on the desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just take a quick look through it and just make sure.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, sir, if you -- if today I asked you the same questions concerning the same matters that are set forth in your statement, would your answers be the same as those that are contained in the statement that you gave to the Gotovina Defence team the week before last? Would they be the same answers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In substance, yes. But to quote word for word, that is something I'm unable to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. None of us can do that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 1D00-0767.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D1425. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit D1425 is admitted into evidence. Under Rule 92 ter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I would like to ask you a couple of question or several questions that are directed to questions that were asked by Mr. Russo over the past several days, and some of them by way of clarification, and that's where I'm going to begin. And I'd like to ask you some questions about the planning for Operation Storm that you discussed with Mr. Russo. And if I can take you to -- this is on page --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Counsel, on page 16262, line 7 and line 9 you noted that the last -- you were asked on line 6: "Q. Can you tell us when planning activity for this operation began?" And Mr. Russo was talking about Operation Storm. The answer was: "The last planning activity for Operation Storm started on July the 31st, 1995, as soon as General Gotovina and I flew back from Brioni to Rujani." There was some request for further clarification, and you noted several lines down from line 13 through to line 18: "Part of the front line from Dinara to Velebit, that was the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District, and after the separation of forces under the Zagreb Agreement, that's when the first planning activity for a possible attack operation began. That's why I'm saying that the day indicated was the last day of activity for Operation Storm." Can we get a bit of clarification on this, Mr. Rajcic, because we're talking about a Zagreb Agreement, I believe is approximately 29th of March, 1994; are you talking about agreement or are you talking about the Vance Plan where the UN came in to monitor occupied territories which was the end of 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that Mr. Kehoe is seeking clarification, however, if you read a bit further down in the citation he was asked for clarification about that particular event --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is cross, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. President, and the clarification in the answer he gives a bit later on is indicated at page 16262 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me, excuse me, [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Please don't cut me off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... please. Mr. Rajcic, could you take your earphones off for a while. Yes. Now, what exactly is your problem Mr. Russo? Is it misrepresenting the answer of the witness, is it -- what exactly is your concern?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe it is misrepresenting or an attempt to misrepresent the answer of the witness. I asked for a clarification about that particular issue. The witness gave a particular answer. He is now being asked to clarify and being directed to a different portion in time, where, if you read the clarification that I engaged in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just then check exactly. First, I'll check the question now put to ... Mr. Kehoe, what happened is Mr. Russo asked questions about planning activities, starting with the 31st of July, and you referred to lines 13 to 18, and you referred to the Zagreb Agreement in 1994, and if I look at the questions put by Mr. Russo on page 16262, your questions could create some confusion, Mr. Kehoe, as to whether we are talking about the same. So would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's what I was going to clarify, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Already in the questions, please, as -- because if the answers were what happened in 1995, and if you want to take him back to -- to another moment, then it should at least be clear that you are talking about something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that's exactly where I was going. I was going back to that time-frame prior to the 31st of July. I mean we're at least going back to 1994 the Zagreb Agreement goes back, as he mentions, in 1994. There is also the separation of forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, of course, you put it in the context of the answers in relation to 1995, and there's as such no problem if there is any specific reason. But there is a risk of creating confusion. Mr. Rajcic, could you put on your earphones again. Please try to formulate your question that every possible confusion is excluded, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic during course of questioning with Mr. Russo you were talking about the planning for Operation Storm beginning on the 31st of July, 1995. Now this was the final planning for Operation Storm, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now there were plans being developed by the HV well prior to that, and I'm talking about military plans, that would use the HV to re-take the Krajina, including Knin, from the Republika Srpska Krajina, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's talk about when those plans began. When -- and put aside the word of Operation Storm because we know from the documents that the term "Operation Storm" didn't come into existence, I believe, until Directive 4 of the Main Staff on 29 June 1995. But let's just talk about the planning by the HV for the re-taking of the Krajina. When did those plans commence? When did they begin?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the first planning started after the Z-4 Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And approximately when was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, in terms of the time, that was in 1994. The spring of 1994, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, are you referring to the Z-4 Plan, or are you referring to the Zagreb Agreement; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am placing this in the context of the Zagreb Agreement, the decision on the separation of forces, the cessation of combat activities, when the army - shall I say - was in a different situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can clarify that yet further. Are you talking about when these plans began at a time when the UN came in and established the Zone of Separation between the Republic of Croatia and the Republika Srpska Krajina? Are you talking about that time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the UN moved in, the agreement, the subsequent mobilisation went from 1991 to 1992; didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first demobilisation. I was then in the area of Dubrovnik. I am talking about the period of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's talk about -- let's go to 1994. Approximately when in 1994 did these plans begin to be developed by the HV for the liberation of the Krajina? When did that happen in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, started what we referred to as staff training, courses for the actual situation. That meant preparing the commands and the units in their respective zones of responsibility to undertake preparatory activities for the moment if it should occur, if the need should arise, that is, to militarily resolve the question of the occupied area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you say that the preparations began, what, in fact, did the HV start to do in 1994 to prepare for the re-taking of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the segment that I was in charge with -- of, the artillery of the Military District of Split, the first steps were training troops, non-commissioned officers, officers, and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in this training of troops and non-commissioned officers and officers, did you also engage in war games and try to plot out exactly how the attack would unfold?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to standard operating procedure, in such activities, the different variants are simulated of a possible action, judging the disposition or estimating -- assisting the -- the disposition of the enemy and his reactions to the different variants of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to this planning as it involves the possible use of artillery. When you are planning going back to 1994, were you planning targets that you could conceivably attack and were you establishing what the X, Y, Z, coordinates were for those targets?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Always. When have you a scenario -- a variant when artillery is concerned, you always work on the basis of available intelligence and inventory or the so-called list of targets as a whole, and then you may -- when you have made a choice of your final variant, the filter variant, as it were, then you define the most important targets for that variant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let's stay with the targets. When you began your planning, sir, certain targets were targets that you had the X-Y-Z coordinates from for a significant period of time such as the headquarters of the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina or the northern barracks or items such as that value; did you not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So would you -- would agree with me there were certain targets such as hard targets like the headquarters that you had those grid coordinates for those types of targets and other targets for a significant period of time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, we will go from the -- just for a moment the theoretical to the practical. In the planning stages, you -- in the army, continuously update your plans, based upon what changes in the battlefield, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do. In fact, 24 hours a day, around the clock, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So for instance if we take into conversation what happened in the Livno valley with Jump 1, Jump 2, and Summer 1994 that would -- excuse me, Summer 1995, apologies, that would cause you to make some updates to the plans that you already had; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going down to the actual practical realities on the battlefield, and let's talk about how things unfold in 1995. The reality was that the confrontation lines remain relatively static except for the area around the Dinara after Jump 1, Jump 2, and Summer 1995; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Jumps 1 and 2, we embarked on Operation Summer 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And my question is the rest of the -- the line, the line covered, for instance, by OG Sibenik or the line covered by OG Zadar those lines remained relatively the same for a significant period of time through 1994 and 1995, up until Operation Storm, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And some from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let's go back to the answer that you gave to the -- to Mr. Russo about the planning, the final planning, on the 31st of July of 1995 for Operation Storm. That final planning that you were doing was primarily updating information that you had for a significant time prior to that, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us go to and talk directly about -- what we now know as Operation Storm, and if we can put up on the screen - and this is the directive from the HV Main Staff of 26 June 1995. I think I referred to -- it as 29 June. My apologies, it's the 26th. You don't have it, sir? I'm going to have to put it up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's D956.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It will come up on the screen in Croatian, Mr. Rajcic. Now, this is the directive that we had talked about previously from the Main Staff, Mr. Rajcic, and what I would like to focus us on you can -- more then welcome to take a look at this, but I want to talk about the artillery issues, as that is your area here. But just let me know if you want to examine this any further. Okay, sir? Now you see in the upper right-hand corner, before we move any further, it does have the commentary Oluja, Storm, you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The documents will follow thereafter with that. Let us turn to page 6 of the English and page 5 of the -- the B/C/S, and I am looking at for some guidance for the Chamber and counsel, bullet point 7 on that. Now, if you could take a look for me at bullet point 7, talking about the artillery and rocket support and going down to the second sentence: "The Main Staff directed that the support should focus on neutralising the Republika Srpska army Main Staff and the 7th Corps command post in Knin, the brigade [sic] command post, concentrations of enemy manpower, armour, and artillery in the area of Knin and Benkovac, including ammunition and fuel depots." So it would be accurate to say, Mr. Rajcic, that as early as the 26th of June, 1995, that the Main Staff was issuing an order to General Gotovina that was to go down to you that you were to focus your efforts on an artillery attack with those particular targets in mind, i.e., the Main Staff, command posts, or concentrations of troops; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you -- in order to accomplish your task, you were being told by the Main Staff that you were to, as part of your artillery attack, to use artillery and rocket support systems to accomplish your goals; isn't that right as well?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those that we had at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let's move down from, again, the larger to the more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let us first take a look at P1125, which is the Kozjak order of General Gotovina. And if we can go three pages in, after the first two cover pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I know you recognise this, Mr. Rajcic. You have talked about this during the course of your reports. This is General Gotovina's order on 1 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn our attention to page 14 in the English, and 13 in the Croatian. And if we can highlight that -- three quarters of the way down. Just blow it up a little bit. We're under the artillery support section of paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you can see that paragraph where it says: "Tasks of the artillery and rocket groups," and General Gotovina writes about using it against the powerful strikes against the enemy front line, three lines down, command posts, communications, et cetera; and it notes by putting the towns of Drvar, Knin, Benkovac Obrovac and Gracac under artillery fire. Before we get to this, it is a fact, Mr. Rajcic, that prior to this order, artillery units in the HV were not permitted to attack these urban areas, Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac, which were within the UN protected areas. They weren't permitted to attack those towns without authorisation from the higher command, were they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this order for the first time changes that, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's when we were in a situation to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I have just one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, on that score, if we can just -- we're going to come back to this in a minute. But on that score, if we can just go back to the directive that we just talked about, D956; and if we could turn to page 5 in the English, page 4 in the B/C/S, if we look at the tasks of the Split Military District, and if we go three quarters of the way down under 3, it notes there that at part of the tasks to the Split Military District were artillery and rockets on Knin and Benkovac; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With those items in mind we take this -- that's in June. We do know that there has been some development in the battlefield from June through Operation Storm - Jump 1, Jump 2, Summer 95 - let us go back to the P1125, and go back to that page 14 on P1125 in the English and 13 in the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just blow up that bottom section again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, so we have in June the 26th of 1995 the Main Staff telling General Gotovina to make plans to put Knin and Benkovac under artillery and rocket fire. And then as we move into Operation Storm we have the Kozjak order which is a bit more sophisticated and adds Obrovac, Drvar, and Gracac to the order; but this is now coming down the chain of command to give the green light for you to implement your plans of predesignated targets to do what you have to do with the artillery; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk about this particular language that's in this document, and we're going to get to your order for artillery in a second. But this is it General Gotovina's order. We're going to get to your attachment in a moment. But just this, you, in fact, drafted this portion of General Gotovina's order, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And approximately when did you do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second version was supposed to be on the 2nd of August. There was a -- the first version and then certain amendments were made to it, and then the second one was supposed to be put into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might just interject. I think Mr. Misetic has a record mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry -- it's not a record mistake. My client doesn't have the right B/C/S page on the screen, and he would like to follow, so if we could ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We're talking about -- it should be -- the item on the screen is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: English started 7th, 7 artillery support whereas we start in the B/C/S halfway that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour we do have the right -- actually dealing with the right page although bullet point 7 starts on the previous page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, this particular order is an order that I applies to the corps level artilleries TR and TRS 1 through 5, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you wrote this in the fashion that you wrote it, you then yourself drafted a specific artillery order which was an attachment to this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just need some clarification. The witness's answer with respect to drafting of this he mentioned the first version and then a second version, but I don't know if there is any clarification whether or not what we're looking at, what version that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is P1125 it's the item that you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But apparently, Mr. Russo, if he refers to the witness talking about different versions, let's try to find out whether P112 is what version, so that we ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you know what version this is, the first or the second?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw on page 1 that the cover page said August 1. And then all of a sudden, next time around, it was August 2. I know that on the 2nd of August we had the final version of the order for the attack Operation Kozjak. I may have been mistaken though. Perhaps we can go back to see whether the date is the 1st or the 2nd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the first page of this document, and I'm talking about the first cover page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd of August. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As we go through the attachments, the first attachment is General Gotovina's order of --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So what we have is General Gotovina's order of the 1st. And then one of the attachments for the 2nd is -- let's turn to D970, which is your order, which is dated the 2nd. We're going put that on the screen, D970. Mr. Rajcic, this is your order of 2 August 1995. And if we can go three pages in on the English, we're talking about paragraph 3: "TRS tasks ..." And we see at the bottom there again you list the towns of Drvar, Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac as the towns to be shelled; do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the last sentence of item 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, before we get into some of these items on here, I just want to go through the -- the chain of this. This order is going down to the corps artillery level, OG Sibenik, OG Zadar or it's going down to and to the TS/TRS levels; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the -- if we look at a different order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I could look at 65 ter 4528.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is an order for offensive operations of the 112th Brigade in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can go to the individual tasks for the 112th, let us turn to page 5 in the English under bullet 6, and page 4 in the B/C/S. Now, if we look at this is, we see this is artillery support and if we could turn the page in the English and scroll down in the B/C/S, I want to see if it is on this page. It's on there. This has tasks for the 112th Brigade which notes that: "During the artillery missile preparation of the attack neutralise and eliminate enemy firing points and manpower, prevent concentration build up, and counter-attack of enemy forces for the purpose of deploying reserve forces." Now again, sir, going from the macro to the -- down to the lower levels as this filters down, your order is then disseminated out and other units get a different type of order, which is much more focussed, don't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we have -- an order here that says nothing about shelling Knin, Drvar, Benkovac, or Obrovac; but we have here is an order by an artillery group to -- to fire on a tactical level in support of troops that happen to be fighting at the ARSK; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think that question, first of all, is argument where it says we see nothing about shelling of Knin, Drvar, Benkovac, or Obrovac, I don't know what that -- other than argument, I'm not sure what that adds to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is to make a distinction between we see what we see in another document and what we see here; and I think that is perfectly reasonable to do. Apart from that you said first -- first of all, argument and then second of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't think I have a second of all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you understand the question, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you answer it for me, with regard to this particular task, being orders issues on a tactical level?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the commander's decision to use the artillery from the organic establishment part of his unit, in order to modulate it as stipulated here in order to perform certain tasks for him at the tactical level. He simply went down to the lowest level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us go back to the order that you issued, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 65 ter 4528.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document shall be given Exhibit D1426.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt there. I just got ahead of myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back to the order of General Gotovina of P1125 again, page 14, and 13 in the Croatian, which has the language of putting these towns under artillery fire. Mr. Rajcic, we are again talking about the sentence in the bottom of number 7, about putting the towns of Drvar, Knin, Benkovac, and Obrovac, and Gracac under artillery fire; do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I put this -- this issue to you, Mr. Rajcic. It is the position of the Prosecution that that particular phraseology was an order to indiscriminately fire on these towns. That is the position of the Prosecutor. What do you have to say about that, and tell us what you believe the intent of this order was.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This formulation is actually to impression upon those of lower rank, subordinates, that is, that in these settlements and towns there were important military units, facilities, and commands; and that with the top level the upper level of the Main Staff, the task had been executed of defining in this specific form when writing the order in this particular bullet point for the corps level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me take this question one step further. Was the intent of this line in the order to fire at pre-planned military objectives; or was it just to fire indiscriminately throughout the town. What was it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard nor ever issued an order to the effect -- to execute indiscriminate fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The other part of my question was so was the intent of this order to fire on pre-planned military objectives that you had -- that you had discussed and planned prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise. It was always implied, understood, as far as I was concerned, in other words, it was mandatory for me that exclusively an only target, a target with specific coordinates. I always maintain that is so, that it is understood, that that is why I do not always explain it at length.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe before we go to the next document, I'd like to take the break now because we need a bit more time for the lunch break today as usually between morning an afternoon session. And I'm looking to everyone in the courtroom. My schedule would be that we'll have a break now until ten minutes to 1.00, that we then have a very short last morning session of approximately half an hour, that we then have one-hour lunch break, so that we resume at a quarter past -- 20 minutes past 2.00. We have a break, and we resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'd just like to begin where we left off with your last statement and on page 70, line 7, you said: "It was always implied understood as far as I was concerned that, in other words, it was mandatory for me that exclusively a target with specific coordinates." Let me -- what you were talking about there is that you believe that every particular target would have specific coordinates upon which to fire upon than was discussed prior to Operation Storm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a brief example of this. Turn your attention to 65 ter 401, which I believe had been a part of the initial exhibit list, but I'm mistaken, it's not there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What I have before you, sir, is regular report for the 4th of August at 0600 hours. You can look at it on your screen by Colonel Vukic from OG Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we go to the second paragraph, and this is a report to the Zadar forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes that artillery support to the attack began at 0500 hours, "Artillery is still firing at the previously selected targets." Now that is consistent with your orders on the use of artillery, that it would be directed at these previously selected targets; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Previously selected target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 65 ter 401.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D1427.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1427 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continuing on, Mr. Rajcic, and I'd like to put to you several positions that have been advanced by the OTP. And the OTP has advanced at various points in this trial the concept or the idea that the intent of the artillery attack by the HV was to shell towns that had no military targets; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They've also noted that the -- and I'm saying that the Office of the Prosecutor has advanced this theory: That the intent of the shelling by the HV in Operation Storm was not to defeat the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina but to force civilians to flee the Krajina; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that ever the intention or was that ever the design of the artillery attack?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us switch subjects to some degree, and I would like to talk with you a little bit about the planning that you engaged in prior to Operation Storm. And I'm talking about the artillery planning, if I was not clear enough. Before I begin that, as a follow-up, was there ever any intent to use artillery to force the civilian population to flee?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I was, that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, if you can -- thank you for the answer. If you can direct your attention to your statement, if I may, and that is D1425, for the record. I want to refer you to several paragraphs in your statement and then ask you a question. I'm not going to quote and read it line by line. It's before the Trial Chamber. But before we do that if I can just follow up on your last answer where you noted that when I asked you was that ever the intent -- was there any intent to use artillery to force the civilian population to flee. And you said: "Where I was, that was not the case." Do you know of any instance during Operation Storm or any other location where that was the intent? Do you know any other part of the HV operation where they did use artillery to get the civilian population to flee?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. However, I categorically assert that I'm not aware of that, only where I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, sir. In paragraph 10 of your statement, you note - I will just paraphrase. You note that artillery was specifically discussed at planning meetings for Operation Storm. If we turn your attention a little bit down to paragraph 15 and 16. You note in paragraph 15 that the most important focus of the artillery was to be the main ARSK headquarters, the communications centre, 7 Krajina Corps headquarters in the northern barracks. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And in paragraph 16, you note and that's the last sentence, that these targets were going to be fired on with T130s and 122 MRLs?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... at this point. Now with your understanding that the 122 MRLs were going to fire on these targets, the specific X-Y-Z coordinates for these objectives were known both to the 4th Guards Brigade and the 7th Guards Brigade, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The coordinates were always known.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn to paragraph 59 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Paragraph 59 discusses a meeting that you had on the 3rd of August, the day before Operation Storm, where you met with TS-3 and the 7th Guards Brigade, and you also had a meeting with the chiefs of artillery of the 7th and 4th Guards Brigade, with the purpose of coordinating artillery support along -- support on the main axis. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, at this time, sir, you understood, did you not, that the northern barracks were going to be the target of MRL fire, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MRL?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Multiple-barrel rocket launchers. The 122 MBRLs.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you knew that the 7th, and possibly the 4th, on orders of the 7th were going to fire on the northern barracks in the early morning hours of the 5th as well as firing on -- at a tactical depth various places where ARSK soldiers were located on the front line; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- let me digress just one second about the use of MRLs and artillery. Not only at the strategic and operational level in depth but also along the front line area at the more of the tactical depth, when you began to fire on the 4th and throughout the 4th, where was most of the fire directed by the HV artillery? Was it directed at the front line area or was it directed at -- in depth in places like the northern barracks or the headquarters? Can you give us an idea of the firing and how it went?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The focus of the use of all the artillery, which was two artillery battalions of the 4th and 7th Guards Brigades, with the support of TS-3, Artillery Group 3, if we leave aside the long-range artillery, 130-millimetre cannon, namely two 130-millimetre cannons deployed in the area of Grahovo. The 155-millimetre Howitzers, three of them are from the -- from the 20th Artillery Battalion, and two 203-millimetre Howitzers from the 20th Howitzer Artillery Battalion, was planned -- or, rather, it was planned that all of them should focus as far as possible the fire from the forward defence line of the enemy into their tactical depth. The rest of the artillery firing from the same direction, and these are the two 130-millimetre cannons I mentioned, and 122-millimetre B-21 launchers, were planned to open artillery fire into the operational depth, where strategic targets were to be found as well. In other words, roughly speaking, two-thirds of all the artillery pieces were used, or perhaps one-fourth, only for the operational depth, and firing upon strategic targets, whereas everything else was in the function -- in the service of routing the first defence line, the first line of deployment of the enemy along the Dinara.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So there was some mixup on the numbers there. So let me get this. Twenty-five percent, you said, is of what you had was fired at the operational depth going after strategic and operational targets; and 75 percent was fired towards the front line area where the confrontation line was; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the artillery attack was being prepared, this is something that was planned, which does not mean that this was indeed the balance of forces in combat. As you can see from the document -- documents, the thrust of the artillery attack of the Croatian army was aimed against the forward line of defence of the enemy and their tactical depth, where their artillery pieces were deployed, as well as the tactical targets which were the command posts of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, before we go any further I want to ask you a couple of questions about the munitions that were used because it has come up during the course of this trial. Now, the MRLs that were available to the HV, did they have a cluster munition to them or were they a standard contact munition?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only multiple rocket launchers but 130-millimetre cannons and Howitzers used contact action projectiles. In other words, there were no cluster munitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me address another issue on these munitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could turn your attention to, if I may, 65 ter 704 -- 7084 -- excuse me, 7083; my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a document that is -- actually the date is illegible but it's a daily operations report. But I would like to get a explanation from you on is in the ammunition section in the middle of the first page. Do you see in the ammunition status there, sir? In the ammunition status there it says TF p/p. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what does that TF p/p, stand for, sir. And when you do that, can you explain the next one which I think should be TF s/p?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not s-e-p, rather, s/p. Or rather not sip but s/p. TF stands for the type of projectile, the type of projectile which was form as a combination of a contact action and fuse projectile for various operative practical and other reasons to make it efficient to fire upon a target. That's how it's been called; p/p means that it is -- it contains a solid charge. In other words, the projectile, 122-millimetre D-30 is the Howitzer involved, has as part of its combat set the possibility for a certain amount of the ammunition contained in the set from the casing of the projectile where the charge is contained, to be -- to have some of the gun powder set aside, in order to fire upon targets that are within shorter range. Something that would otherwise have been impossible by merely using p/p charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't think that came across -- I don't think that came across in the translation. If Mr. Misetic can clear this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, p/p there was a different interpretation. It's at page 77, line 21, if I could just say it again and see if ... it will make more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we might have some difficulties in guiding the witness in this very technical matter. Mr. Russo, I take it that the assistance of Mr. Misetic is appreciated by you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The phrase p/p I believe the witness indicated means "puno punjenje."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, it could be interpreted as full charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say, Mr. Rajcic, that the p/p means full charge and the s/p stands for half charge?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Reduced charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And those designations bear on the range of that particular weapon, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So in -- if in any of these documents p/p is translated as anti-personnel shells, that would be incorrect; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time subject to changes in the translation, we will offer into evidence 65 ter 7083. The translation that I'm talking about is on the top line where it notes the p/p is a anti-personnel shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is no objection. I note the document is attachment 17 to P2339, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit D1428.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And a corrected translation will then be uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we notice we will upload and change that. We have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and you communicate with the Registrar on uploading a new English translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I say please proceed. I think I said that we would try to finish at 20 minutes past 1.00 and have a very short last session. Could you give us an indication as what time you would still need after our lunch break, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Half an hour, at the outset, 45 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider this request. We'll have a break, and we resume at 20 minutes past 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, we had previously, prior to the break, been talking a little bit about MRLs and their use on predesignated targets, and I'd like to touch on a subject with you that was brought up on direct examination, and that is the Ivancica map, the coded map that was on P2338. If we could bring that up on the screen, Mr. Usher? Now, if we could just leave it in that context, then. You were asked some questions on this map with regard to the use of the 122 multi-barrelled rocket-launchers, but I would like to just ask you some general questions about these coded maps to begin with. Now, this coded map is not a map that's exclusively used in the artillery setting, is it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what these coded maps are generally used for?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are maps that are used as auxiliary resources attached to the planning documentation in the armed forces. They were primarily used for the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's take that one step further. You're using it primarily for infantry, but it's used for coded communications in the infantry, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the documents, the function of which is inter alia communication amongst all the protagonists of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you're using these coded maps, I mean, these circles are reference points, aren't they? I mean, they aren't specific targets, are they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Reference points, yes, but this can be circled with the disposition of, for instance, the firing position -- positions of the artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. Now, this type of map, I mean, this map is put together before operational planning, planning for a particular operation; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this type of a map is always in use, also at the time when the units are in the preparation stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, I mean, the map is -- this map is put together. You have these codes put in there for the infantry to use, and thereafter then you begin your particular operation and planning and decide on your particular artillery targets, et cetera; is that how it goes?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on the basis of these maps that the targets are defined for artillery, those targets which are located within the circle or in its immediate vicinity; of the circle, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We're going to talk about those individual targets, because that takes me to something you said during the course of your testimony with Mr. Russo. But before we get to that: When was this coded map created; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is Ivancica, this was used by the 7th Guards Brigade and it was created for Operation Oluja, Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us go back to your statement about targets within circles. And if I could go back to something that you said on Friday, and that's -- this is on page 16410. You've noted that on line 20: "These maps were made, as far as I know, with the final modifications in 1996 and 1998. The former JNA did not plot its installations into military maps." So when we go down to the area around 16, if we could just, you know, drift down into 16, which is in the lower half of this to the left of that solid line, okay, in that area that's around "16," sir -- can you -- let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's further down. Yes, it's further down. Keep going. It's further up, yeah. Can you go back up? Sorry, it's down. Where is it? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you looking for "Knin"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay it's on the circle on the right. Just go to the area that's on the right around Knin. It's in that circle around Knin. There we go. And we see "S-16" there in the middle. If we can just blow that up a little bit. Now, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted for us that the northern barracks is not plotted on this coded map, is it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this goes back to what you said, that the basis of this is this is an old JNA map and they didn't put those old facilities on there; is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think it's unclear -- well, first of all, the witness said "If this is the Ivancica map" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I think the best way of doing it is to refer to pages and to lines, rather than to whisper in the ear of the witness what is important for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. At page 3, line 1, the witness indicates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have here in front of me, page 3, line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm with you. Page 3, line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And this is where the witness indicated when the map was created or what it was created for, and then Mr. Kehoe brought him back to something he had said on Friday. So I think there is -- needs some clarification of which one it is, if this is the map he's referring to at page 3, line 1, or if this is another kind of map created at a different time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fair, Mr. President. I'll clarify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we need to be a little clearer on what we're talking about. The underlying map is a JNA map; isn't that right? Let's put the circles aside. The underlying map is a JNA map; right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: JNA? Can I have an explanation, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The Yugoslav National Army.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the underlying map is the JNA map, yes, the topographic map of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that's the map that was made back in 1996, or 1998, or, excuse me, even well prior to that, I'm sorry, and it was made prior to Operation Storm, right, the JNA map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I have correctly replied to the question. Can I have a Croatian translation, please? The last amendments to these maps, the JNA maps, were in 1978.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from that particular map, the 7th Guards Brigade put circles on this map for the purposes of Operation Storm; right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry that took so long to get there, but -- and in these underlying JNA maps, you noted for us previously, on page 16410, that they didn't include military installations; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that military facilities were not marked on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you noted for us that, for instance, when you look at the map that's on the screen, the Ivancica map, that map does not have the northern barracks designated, does it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can I digress somewhat?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have one such original map in my brief-case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's just deal with this one. This particular map doesn't have the northern barracks on it, does it, the Slavko Rodic Barracks?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't say this -- this original one, without the circles, without the military installations, military facilities, drawn in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Without going through what the witness has in his suitcase, he was talking about a geographical map. If it's purely geographical, then of course you would find roads, railways, et cetera, but that's it. If it's more than geographical, then of course we could look at the map he apparently has in his suitcase, so he has a good impression of what was the basis on which one worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think that -- I'm not sure exactly I know what you're referring to. I'm just looking at the exhibit that was presented during direct examination, which was this particular map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but apparently conclusions -- or at least it apparently has some relevance, what was indicated on the maps on which these maps were based. If it's purely geographical, then I wouldn't expect anything else than perhaps buildings or -- but not specific indications, other than, I would say, features as you see them from the air, without any explanation; so therefore, since you're asking what was on the original maps and what was not, it seems to have some relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, actually, with this particular map, I'm asking is the northern barracks designated now going to the other military facilities. It's got no military features --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I keep in the back of my mind whether it would assist me and perhaps my colleagues to see the map on the basis of which this one was produced. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, this map doesn't have a facility marked for, for instance, the southern barracks or the Senjak barracks either; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this map would have no information on military features or military buildings that are located in this -- in the Knin area, would it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barracks, not only the Main Staff, which should be recognised in this area because it is marked, just like all other facilities are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But clearly the northern barracks and the Senjak Barracks are not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if you were to -- using an artillery map, an artillery map with X-Y-Z coordinators would, of course, be different from this coded map, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, you would have tabular textualar -- there would be a tabular textualar list with those coordinates on it, would there not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that particular coordinate that was fired upon by the brigades, that is the type of information you covered with the 4th and 7th Guards Brigade prior to the firing on the northern barracks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- I'm sorry. Now, when you looked at this map, you looked at the map at S-16 and you noted, based on the diary, that the target was the northern barracks because you knew that target was to the right of S-16; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you knew, from your own personal knowledge, that that was the particular area where the multi-barrelled rocket-launchers were fired into; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, of course, that, without going into this again, was based on what you said previously, the discussion of the X-Y-Z coordinates with the 4th and 7th Guards Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me put to you what the Prosecutor's allegation concerning S-16 is. The Prosecutor's allegation is that the HV intentionally fired into a residential area that is designated here as S-16. That is the position of the Prosecution that's before this Chamber, and my question to you, Mr. Rajcic, is: Is that true? Did, in fact, the HV fire into a residential area with multi-barrelled rocket-launchers either on the 4th or the 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Explain to me the basis of your position. Explain to the Chamber, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the precise coordinates that we have, X, Y and Z, were placed on the map, we would have a clearer picture of where the center of the target was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was the northern barracks, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just have one moment here. Let me turn our attention briefly to one last document in this area before we move off into the final brief area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe. Before we leave this, and the map is now on our screen: Mr. Rajcic, could you tell us where apparently it was intended to fire to the right of 16, what did 16 depict? I mean, why was there a circle there? What was the purpose of plotting 16 on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When infantry units, for their own purposes and needs, mark significant features or facilities in the course of combat, then they have a different approach, and when on this base the target is shown, then S-16 would be the reference point indicating where the artillery target, in fact, is. So when something is to the right of S-16, when it is stated barracks to the right of S-16, then we have the location of the barracks in this space as being between S-16, S-13, and S-17, and S-21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what now is S-16 plotted for on this map? I mean, what is it? Why if you put a circle around a certain matter that is because you want to indicate something? Now, it apparently is not the northern barracks as a target for artillery, it's something else. Could you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It marks the place where infantry units would, at a certain point during combat, find themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you talking about your own troops or about troops from -- enemy troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both. My own troops, too, my own units, too, when an inhabited place is entered into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then again, I mean, it's not the whole of the town, which is in one big circle, but there are all circles apparently not put at random on this map. And you earlier said that the map indicated all kind of facilities. Now, my question is: What does S-16 stand for, other than it covers an area? I mean, what's the relevance of that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, according to my own orientation, S-16 would also cover the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, S-16 covers the police station. That's -- well, that's -- so, therefore, can I take it that all these marked circles, circles numbered by -- all these circles that are numbered, they all stand for something, some relevant feature, whatever that may be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The orientation point can be a river crossing, an intersection, an elevation, a railway crossing, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not exclude so the relevance, then, is that's where there's a railway crossing, but so there's always something relevant to be found for which that circle is plotted on this map? It's not at random, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They're not random, but the density is such that the infantry units must show -- must indicate where they are deployed in order to avoid any misunderstandings in communication at the level of infantry units and for the purpose of seeking support from other branches, in this case possibly also the artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could just go one step further, let's use the hypothetical. We are infantry that's in the area, and we have Motorolas that we're talking on, and you, Mr. Rajcic, ask me, Where are you? And I say, I'm in S-6. You then go to this map, and you would see that where I am along the Krka River on S-6; isn't that how it works?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then you might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For such purposes, what would grid references not do? Because here, if they are -- if you just have to tell someone where you are, then it comes a bit as a surprise that we have not all adjacent circles. And earlier, I think you said that these depict facilities. Whatever that facility would be, unless you earlier said crossroads or whatever? I mean, these circles, are they exclusively for locating persons who are moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Primarily, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge asked about grid references. Now, grid reference is something that is not coded, is it? I mean, the grid reference is -- the X-Y-Z grid reference are grid reference that everybody knows about, the RSK side, the HV side, the VRS side, they all know what X-Y-Z grid references are; right? This coded map -- you have to say yes or no, sir. I mean, I know you're shaking your head yes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your point is clear, Mr. Kehoe, to the extent you wanted to draw the attention of the Chamber to the fact that a coded map would need a key to understand communications, that's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and so it's clear, it's, for instance, Mr. President, you and I were talking -- if I can have the witness take his headphones off. I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take your headphones off for a while, Mr. Rajcic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you and I are talking with a coded map, you have a copy of the coded map, I have a copy of the coded map, you ask me, Where are you. I give you my location of S-6 or S-16, or anywhere else on there, you and I both know where we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just explaining that that was understood; so, therefore, to ask the witness to take his earphones off and to explain to me what I showed already to have understood is -- take some time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The takeoff point was just your issue on grid references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, could you put on your earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I asked you previously whether or not there was an attempt, as presented by the Prosecutor, to fire into residential areas with multi-barrelled rocket-launchers, and you said, "No." Let me direct your attention to D389, which is an intelligence report from the ARSK from the morning of the 4th of August, 1995. If you could take a quick look at this, sir, I'm not certain if -- can you read this, sir? If not, I will read the English, the pertinent English paragraph. I ask that question because I know it's in Serbian Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read Cyrillic, but it will take me a while longer because it's more difficult for me to perceive the letters. Well, I can see "Knin, Drvar, Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac." What passage are you referring me to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm referring you to the fourth paragraph down, where it says that: "Knin was attacked from Livanjsko Polje from several directions, from time this information was drafted, between 200 and 300 rounds of different calibres impacted on the town. The first strike was carried out on the building of the SVK General Staff, which suffered great material damage with the fleet of vehicles almost completely destroyed. Later the fire was transferred on the military barracks, the 1300 "kapalara," [phoen] the TVIK factory, the railway intersection, residential buildings in the area beneath the Knin fortress ..." Are you with me, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, that is consistent with how this -- the attack went, isn't it, in the sense of the artillery prep first fired on the General Staff and other locales, and it was thereafter, for instance, shortly thereafter, that the order was given to redirect that fire on the TVIK factory; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, yes, the order is 130, and the barracks and the Main Staff were targeted at the same. Could you please explain to me where it says between 200 and 300 impacts? Impacts of what? I didn't understand that. It says here "projectiles," and I understood you to have said something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There may be a translation issue. My English copy says "200 and 300 rounds of different calibres." That just happens to be the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says here the first impact or the first strikes was on the Army of Republika Srpska, where severe damage was caused, and the fleet of vehicles was almost completely wiped out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And my question on this score, Mr. Rajcic, is: This particular intelligence report is consistent with how you structured the artillery prep in attacking first the headquarters, for instance, and the communications centre, and thereafter, for instance, the TVIK factory; it's consistent with that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is in line with the prioritisation of targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us change to one last topic, sir, and it has to do with the issue of General Gotovina as the operational commander or General Gotovina as an operational commander in Operation Storm, and for reference purposes I'm talking about page 16454 at line 13 down to line 17. And you were asked, during the course of direct examination by Mr. Russo whether General Gotovina was the operational commander during Operation Storm, and you asked for some clarity, but let me just take this one step further. General Gotovina was the operational commander for the joint HV/HVO forces that had moved up through the Livno Valley in Jump 1, Jump 2, Summer of 1995, as well as Operation Storm, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't get an interpretation of the last part. There was some interruptions in the interpretation, so I didn't get the full interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the whole of the question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General Gotovina was the operational commander of all Croatian forces during Jump 1, Jump 2, and Summer 95, as well as Operation Storm, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And after Operation Storm and the Croatian forces, and I say "the Croatian forces," I mean HV and HVO, not just HV - HV and HVO - after they began to move into Bosnia for Operational Mistral and Southern Movement, General Gotovina continued as the operational commander for all Croatian forces both HV and HVO, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for all Croatian forces, I received interpretation "southern movement," and it was "southern axis," not for the full -- entire force of the HVO, but only for elements of the HVO, some units of the HVO that had joined into the Croatian Army, and together they formed Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
