utterances.text: And those elements that joined the Croatian forces were there for all the activities through Operation Storm and then obviously the activities in Operation Mistral and Operation Southern Movement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document that we'll review via Sanction, and if we could just put this on the screen via Sanction. We, in fact, have a hard copy, if the witness wants to look at a hard copy. Have you taken a look at that, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a general question concerning this document that is a protocol from 25 November 1995, in the -- excuse me, September 1995 in Novi Travnik, 25 September 1995; and it notes the Croatian forces, and these Croatian forces -- that these officers that we have listed here encompass not only HV forces but HV officers as well, don't they -- HVO officers, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: For instance, Major General Filip Filipovic, because he was HVO at this time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miljenko Filipovic, that's what it should say. As far as I know, I think that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in this particular context, I mean, when General Gotovina is the commander of all Croatian forces, both HV and HVO, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that the general makes a decision to create a team from both components that would escort him to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I get -- what I'm talking about, as we move through the entire fighting that was going on, and he was the commander of Croatian forces, both HV and HVO, as he signs it for the Croatian forces, if you see on the second page, when he's signing it for the Croatian forces, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that he was the most responsible person here, the commander, the supreme commander for this thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we do not have a dock ID number for this, I don't believe. If we could MFI it at this point while we get a dock ID, we'd be -- appreciate that and offer it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we reserve an MFI number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit D1429, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar, and that's the 25th of September document, a protocol of the meeting between representatives of the Croatian forces and the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Rajcic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic, who's counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will be speaking the same language, and in cases such as this, I have to ask you to take into account the interpreters. That means that you have to wait a while after I finish my question so that the interpreters are given an opportunity to interpret everything for the record. Mr. Rajcic, in the course of your testimony, we heard about your function, we heard about the tasks that you carried out, we heard a number of explanations that you provided to us, and it will greatly assist the Trial Chamber, I'm sure. We may be repeating ourselves and going through some of the ground that has already been covered, but the context is going to be somewhat different. Mr. Rajcic, Operation Storm was carried out in the UN Sector South, and this area was, in fact, an area where two operational zones were in existence, Gospic and Split; that's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Military District of Gospic, which was under the command of General Norac, and the Split Military District, which was under the command of General Gotovina, had a certain territory which was defined before Operation Storm was launched; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And both Military District Commanders had, as their immediate superior, the Chief of General Staff, General Cervenko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Given this organisational structure, I think that you've already told us this, but let us repeat it, it was impossible for one commander issues orders to units of the other military district. For instance, was it possible for General Norac, who commanded the Gospic Military District, to issue orders to units that were within the Split Military District?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Hypothetically speaking, if there was a need for this kind of command to be exercised, it could only be done through the chief of the General Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In this area between the two military districts, there were the special police units of the Ministry of the Interior under the command of General Markac; they were operating there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you know that the special units of the police were subordinated to the Main Staff, to the chief of the Main Staff, pursuant to the recommendations or the suggestions of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, President Tudjman, and with the approval of both ministries, the Defence Ministry and the Ministry of the Interior; were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw anything of the kind in writing anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But as regards the exercise of command, I think that you said in your previous testimony that just as the Commander General Gotovina could not exercise command over units in the Gospic Military District, he could not exercise command over the special police units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'd like to just clarify something. The witness was asked about the converse situation, whether Norac could command individuals in the Split Military District. It's now put to him the converse of that, which is General Gotovina commanding people in the Gospic Military District. I don't know if that particular part was ever put to him. In other words, only one half of that two possible scenarios was actually put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit it's not entirely clear, what you're aiming at, Mr. Russo, but if Mr. Mikulicic says he can clarify, he apparently understands, and then you have an opportunity to intervene at a later stage if need be. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, perhaps I went too quickly. When I asked you whether General Norac could exercise command over units in the Split Military District, you said that he couldn't, but the converse was also true; General Gotovina could not exercise command over the Gospic Military District units?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless there were proper orders issued by the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Now, as regards the special police units that were under the command of General Markac, and we said that he was subordinated to the chief of the Main Staff, it's the same situation, in fact?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the directive stipulated this in that manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, did you personally see any orders whereby General Gotovina would order anything to the special police units, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When we spoke earlier in the examination-in-chief -- or, rather, when you, Mr. Rajcic, spoke about a specific military term, "resubordination," correct me if I'm wrong, if I interpret -- misinterpret your words, you said that this can only be done in combat where the Commander-in-Chief or the Supreme Commander may issue an order placing a unit under the command of another military formation? Did I interpret your words correctly?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, resubordination is an action of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, does that mean that when the Supreme Commander orders a unit to be resubordinated, that the unit can be resubordinated only within the units that are under the command of that commander that we're talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: For instance -- let us go back to this topic. For instance, General Gotovina, could he issue an order resubordinating, for instance, the 2nd Battalion of the 9th Guards Brigade to General Norac without the approval of the chief of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for these answers. I shall now like to ask the Registry to bring up Exhibit D543. Mr. Rajcic, we shall shortly see coming up on the screen an order by the commander of the Main Staff, general of the armies, Zvonimir Cervenko of 29 July 1995, addressed to the commander of the special forces of the Ministry of the Interior, Colonel General Mladen Markac. Let me, first of all, ask you whether you had occasion to see this order.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Allow me to draw your attention to the part of the order which is contained in item 2 of the second paragraph, where General Cervenko orders this: "In the first stage, with tactical surprise, by committing forces of adequate strength with considerable artillery support from our own forces and reached the Sveti Rok ..." And it goes on to specify the actual points on Mount Velebit; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, as the artillery chief of the Military District of Split, were you acquainted with the fact that the special police had also its own artillery at disposal in action?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the artillery which was for the level of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Am I interpreting your answer correctly if I say that colloquially this is short-range artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mortar, 82-mm, 60-mm and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If we take a look at page 2 of this order, item 4, by General Cervenko, we shall see that he says in this order that in the conduct and preparation of combat preparation, work should be constantly coordinated with the Command of the Split Military District, in particular with the Zadar Forward Command Post and the Gospic Forward Command Post?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, how would you explain this word, this phrase that work should be coordinated?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coordination implies the flow of information required with the left and right adjacent or neighbouring units in order to achieve a synchronised unfolding of the combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, Mr. Rajcic, look at this. This was sent, this order, to the commanders of both military districts, Split and Gospic, that is, and now we shall revert to what I said before. You can see that the order was also co-signed, and we managed to decipher the signature through the testimony of a witness, by the deputy Minister of the Interior, Zeljko Tomjenovic [phoen], he -- stating that he agreed to the use of the forces of police stations?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it, but if you say that it has been deciphered as such, then that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have document D1094 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting, I'm going to tell you what you will be seeing on the screen shortly. You will see also an order by General Zvonimir Cervenko which was issued a day later, which is to say on the 30th of July, which order was addressed to the attention of the commander of the Military District of Split. Pay attention to bullet point 4 -- item 4 of this order, which says: "Forces which are active on the slopes of Velebit -- with the forces active on the slopes of Velebit --" or, rather: "Provide the forces engaged on the slopes of Velebit with a special artillery group that will provide them and the MUP forces with artillery support." When General Cervenko here uses the words "those forces," he's obviously referring to HV forces, is he not? And at the same time -- and he uses a conjunction there, "in between the forces of the Ministry of the Interior," so obviously these are two formations of forces. On the one hand, we have the HV forces; and on the other, the MUP forces. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I read it, yes, it does refer to that, as you're saying, to the Velebit forces, to the forces which are on Mount Velebit, plus the MUP forces, the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is known, Mr. Rajcic, that on the slopes of Velebit, there were, in coordinated action, the HV forces and MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in coordinated, concerted action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document P1125 on the screen, please. We shall now see an order for an attack by General Gotovina of the 2nd of August, 1995, which we have already had occasion to see today, and I should like to ask you to focus on page 11 of the Croatian version of this order, which refers to the tasks of the Zadar Operative Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Rajcic, that the Operations Group of Zadar was the force of the Split Military District which, amongst others, was also active on the slopes of Velebit?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You see from the text of this order that the support -- I mean artillery support is rendered by Rocket Artillery Support Group 5?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And also you see what the targets of it is, and it is in the paragraph which starts -- under this paragraph which says that the 2nd Battalion of the 9th Guards Brigade have the task to rout the enemy with the 1st Combat echelon, break up the enemy along the first line of defence, and as soon as possible, cut the Gracac-Obravac road and take control of the Muskovci area. And the last sentence says that they were to secure the right flank of the Special Police of the Ministry of the Interior. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. Can we now have document P1263.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Here we observed -- we noticed that the Rocket Artillery Group 5's task was to provide support to forces that were offensive action on the slopes of Velebit, with their aim being to cut the Gracac-Obravac communication route. What we see now, Mr. Rajcic, is the order for an offensive operation of the 3rd of August, 1995, order for attack, which was issued Mladen Fuzul, Lieutenant-Colonel Mladen Fuzul, the commander of the Zadar Operations Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see chapter 6 of this order, which in the Croatian text is on page 4, which is the chapter on artillery support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So Lieutenant-Colonel Mladen Fuzul, the commander of the Zadar Operations Group, commands thus: In units which are executing offensive operations, artillery groups should be formed of own artillery resources which are to be grouped to focus on the task of the unit with the aim of effective and precise impact on the enemy. And a bit later, for precise fire on the enemy. And later it says in Operation Group Zadar, an Artillery Group 5 should be set up comprising -- and then it goes on to enumerate all the difference ordinance, five T 130-mm field guns, two H 122-mm Howitzers, and one 122-mm multiple rocket-launcher. So do you agree, Mr. Rajcic, that this order actually operationalises practically the order of the chief of the Main Staff on the forming of operational groups, i.e., the support -- artillery support to be rendered to such artillery groups? Is this conclusion of mine correct, from the military standpoint?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not completely, not entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to correct me?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the first documents on coordination and the responsibility zones between the coordinated units is something that I have not seen as yet. Secondly, the slopes of Mount Velebit, we can read here in the order, this is a facility exclusively for the Military District of Split, meaning that the responsibility zone -- it is in the responsibility zone of the left adjacent unit. When they say provide artillery support to those forces on Mount Velebit and to the forces of the special MUP units, I didn't see that then. Thirdly -- sorry, on the 3rd of August at 945 hours, we had a meeting at General Gotovina's office in Zadar, attended by General Markac, and I believe Mr. Sacic was there and the chief of artillery of the special MUP units as well. This model of modulating and organisation of the artillery group, what it should say actually is "artillery rocket group," was drawn up a day before. At that meeting, General Gotovina told me that the order of the chief of Main Staff, General Cervenko, was for me to single out a part -- a segment -- a portion of the artillery resources from the artillery or, rather, Artillery Rocket Group 5 for the requirements of General Markac's units. At that moment, that was quite disruptive of the situation in the area, as far as I was concerned. I understood that oral order then -- of course, we have to take into account the time that has elapsed since. I understood it to mean that those resources were to be attached to the special MUP forces, specifically three 130-mm cannon in the Rovanska disposition area, then Howitzers of 120-mm, D-30, which are resources of the 3rd Guards Brigade of the HVO, and the personnel was to have been from the 112th Brigade of the Croatian Army. And, finally, a launcher, a 122-mm BM-21 launcher which, on the 3rd of August, in the evening, was transported -- relocated from the area of Livno-Lusnic [phoen] to the area of Rovanska to provide support to General Markac's units. Excuse me, allow me. When we read it like it is put here, this structure, I physically could not have changed the documents because we had a few hours at our disposal in which to prepare or start the attack, so that it remained as is, the dates being from the 2nd of August, when I did not have an information or an order to the effect of my having to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic, thank you for this answer. Now I shall like to ask you to take a look at another document which is associated with this, which is P1201. This is an order for attack, and it is the segment dealing with the artillery which was issued by the chief of artillery of Operation Group Zadar, Captain Marijan Firs [phoen], and it is dated the 3rd of August, 1995. And you can see under the very introduction under item 1, under B, that it orders the establishment of Artillery Groups 5 with five 130 cannon, two 122 Howitzers, and three 122 Howitzers, and the multiple rocket-launcher, and the 1st Lieutenant Ante Kardum is the commander. If you look in the second page of the document, we shall see in item 3 what the tasks are. So the task is to mount fierce artillery attacks to break up, neutralise, and destroy the enemy combat disposition at tactical and operational levels and to focus artillery attacks on the locations of Mali Golic, Prezid, Gracac, Islam Latinski, and Debelo Brdo. If we look at item 5, the order states in which way communications are to be organised up to the level of the Artillery Rocket Group, according to the OG Zadar chief of communications plan, and in item 6 the order states that the -- in item 7, sorry, it is stated that chiefs of artillery should elaborate their respective operational groups at their level for the necessary documents for the operation. Is this, Mr. Rajcic, in keeping with your own recollection of the events, given the fact that 15 years have elapsed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not in line with what I recall of artillery developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at D1095. It's a document dated the 4th of August. It was drafted by Colonel Mladen Fuzul, the commander of the Zadar Operations Group, and it is entitled "Daily Combat Report." So this is, in fact, what was done in the field; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the large penultimate passage that begins with the words: "The support in Gracac and in the depth for the special units of the MUP were provided by 130-mm guns and 122-mm Howitzers in the 1st Sector." The fact that the multiple rocket-launcher and ammunition were late in arriving made the support weaker. At around 1300 hours, there was a disruption at the 130-mm gun, and this was repaired at 1800 hours. Again at around 1642 hours, the Howitzers also -- the Howitzer also broke down, and it was still being repaired. It was a 203-mm Howitzer. The entire day, the artillery was engaged in targets at the front line and the area deep behind the enemy lines. Mr. Rajcic, so this was the situation on the first day of Operation Storm, as regards, of course, OG Zadar. Does this report conform with your recollection of that time? Did the weapons break down?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It happened in not only Zadar Operations Group but also in the Sibenik and North Operations Groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, were there situations where ammunition was late in arriving to the positions where the artillery men were engaging their targets?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the ammunition for the launcher was late. This launcher was transferred from Rrazunac [phoen] to Seline, and ammunition was late also on the axis of where the 7th Guards Brigade was attacking. Again it was for 122-mm launchers, BM-21 launchers, so the 7th Guards Brigade borrowed some rockets, rockets from the 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The artillery pieces that we're talking about, the 130-mm cannon and Howitzers, that's long-range artillery, that's corps-level artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's partly true, but the 130-mm cannon and 122 Howitzers, that's brigade artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The targets that these artillery pieces were engaging were selected in the course of the preparations for the operation on the basis of the intelligence and all the other data that the commanders were taken into account when preparing this operation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, overall, but if you're talking about this narrow area, then there is another explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I was talking about the corps artillery, the corps-level artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the corps-level artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And the brigade-level artillery, at the lower level, did it also have pre-selected targets that it was supposed to engage?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the 60-mm mortars to the corps-level artillery, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: However, in the course of combat, resistance points were springing up and new targets were cropping up that could not have been predicted. What was the procedure then, in terms of orders for the use of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Newly-discovered targets, of course, this is something that happens, and then this is communicated to the unit that is capable, in terms of its equipment and operationally, to engage the new target and neutralise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So we can say that the elements of the corps-level artillery providing support on the axes where operations groups were being -- were active, that these are the artillery and Rocket Groups 1 through 5 were not under the command of the commanders of the operational groups; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both yes and no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You'll have to explain this?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, first I said no and then yes, otherwise I would have said yes and then no, because there is an explanation behind all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about the fact that the operational group commanders could not issue direct orders for them to engage targets, but they could request support, and then in line with the situation in the field, the support would be approved by the military district command? Was this how the corps-level artillery operated?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that I will be able to explain this to you because we speak the same language. This was the -- a centralised/decentralised command, it was a mixture. Let me explain. At the operational level and for strategic targets, the commander superior to the operational group is in charge of them. Now, as for the targets that are within the tactical depth of a unit engaged in combat, the commander of the operational group or of the Home Guards Regiment or Brigade can get a unit and direct fire. This is why I say that this was a centralised/decentralised model.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, it may seem illogical to ask lay persons, but I'm sure the Trial Chamber will be able to grasp all that.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, when I talked about resubordination, then it is more difficult for me to explain this. This is, in fact, easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. But, Mr. Rajcic, be that as it may, commanders of the Artillery Rocket groups --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry for rising. If we can check the witness's answer at page 31, line 25, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you have to move to the other one because the system -- one screen -- you said page 31?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, line 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rajcic, you said the commander of the operational group or of the Home Guards Regiment or brigade can get a unit and direct fire, and then our transcript continues with "this is why I say that this was a centralised/decentralised model." Something missing, Mr. Misetic, or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just want to do make sure that's what the witness's answer was. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I just read to you, does that reflect the answer you gave, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this model applied, and I tried to explain it in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, when we're talking about the commanders of the artillery and rocket groups, even before Operation -- before engaging in combat, they had information about the targets, but they did plot their own maps, work maps, so to speak, and they also had the artillery targets as they operated those groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but those were not just work maps. They had to do plans for their engagements, but the plan is not binding. It is again auxiliary material, as it was in my case, it is auxiliary material that just assists one in one's work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, in the analysis that you did last October, I saw that as you commented on the documents that you were able to find, you stated that you had had some problems with the documents that pertained to the functioning and operation of the TS-5, the Artillery Group 5, for the dates 8th and 9th of August; 6, 7 and 8 August, you say that according to your information, that group was not active on those dates; is this the correct conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a small correction. I said, I believe - I don't want to go checking now - that on the basis of the documents at my disposal, I could not reconstruct the activities of Artillery Group 5. Let me repeat, sir. I would like to stress, once again, this material is subject to change for reasons that I indicated, because documents come in all the time and this changes the relations, and so that is why this is not relevant for this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Rajcic. So this material is subject to changes if any missing documents crop up. Mr. Rajcic, thank you very much for your answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. The Cermak Defence show no questions. Mr. Russo, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour. However, I believe the Chamber needs to make a ruling with respect to one matter before I decide exactly how to proceed, probably best discussed outside the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we allow the witness already to have his break. Mr. Rajcic, could you already follow Madam Usher. We'll have a break of approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I have only very brief questions in re-direct. However, the matter of whether or not I am permitted to cross-examine or required to cross-examine the witness on the particular issue of the intent behind Operation Storm, if the Court were to find that that was outside the scope of my direct examination, then I believe I'm required, under Rule 90(H), since I will be in cross-examination, to put to him what we believe the intent of the operation was. However, if the Court feels that that was -- fell within the scope of my direct examination, then I would not be going into those matters in terms of cross-examination. I would simply stick to the re-direct that has come out of what Mr. Kehoe and Mr. Mikulicic referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, quite clearly, if we're going into that, I do not believe the intent was squarely put to the witness. I attempted to do that during counsel's direct examination, and I asked the Court to order the Chamber -- to order the OTP to do that. I understand why the Court did not. Nevertheless, we did put it to the witness, and it is in the 92 ter statement, D1425. If it's intended to be touched upon, then of course Rule 90(H)(2)(i) comes in and the Prosecution should put in exactly what the -- what the Rule says: "Counsel shall put to the witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness." That's what's required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might not always be easy to determine exactly where your question will relate or will be a response to what was put in the 92 ter statement and was not yet covered by your examination-in-chief because, of course, we find elements in the 92 ter statement which are not -- or are not directly covered in the examination-in-chief, dare, I think -- that's to some extent done in a 92 ter statement, where it's put apparently to the witness what was the Prosecution's case. Now, to the extent that matters in a 92 ter statement are not covered by your examination-in-chief, I think you find yourself in a position more or less as a cross-examining party on that issue. Now, to give a ruling is not easy, because it might differ. So if you want to put questions in a certain area, perhaps you indicate, prior to putting those questions, whether you consider this to be a matter on which you cross-examine or whether it's a matter that requires re-examination on the basis of having introduced the matter in chief, questions put in relation to that by the Defence, and now because it came up in cross as a response rather than as a new element, that you either re-examine or cross-examine the witness on that. Am I clear enough? Most likely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President. If I were not on cross-examination with respect to the issue of intent, whether the -- I think this actually arises out of paragraph 9 of the 92 ter statement. However, Mr. Kehoe did ask additional questions about it. If I were in the position of cross-examination as to that particular issue, then I think I would be required to put to him what we believe the intent of the operation was. If I'm not required to do that, if the Court doesn't find that that fell outside the scope, then it's not my intention to put it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may just -- it is two separate provisions under 90(H). One is cross-examination that is on the elements brought up in direct. That's in (2)(i); (2)(ii) is a separate obligation that requires the Prosecution to put its case to the witness, not just the intent element, not just the element that was covered during the course of my examination. It requires the cross-examiner to put the nature of the case to the witness, and the Prosecution should not be limited to just the intent element: Put the case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have any problem putting the case to the witness. The issue is that 90(H) only applies about cross-examination, and if I'm cross-examining, that's fine. The issue is: Where does cross-examination apply and where does simple re-direct apply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that, of course, depends on the questions that you are putting, and it also depends on our interpretation. But, of course, you could assist the Chamber in forming an opinion on that, on whether what Mr. Kehoe asked the witness was in cross-examination of the examination-in-chief or whether he brought up new matters, whether in examining the witness or whether in a 92 ter statement. Mr. Kehoe has very specifically put to the witness that it was the Prosecution's case that a certain intent was there, which gave me the impression that you were eliciting evidence from the witness not in cross-examination, but rather that you sought to elicit evidence as Rule 90(H) says, and I have to find the exact language, that you were seeking evidence relevant to the case of the cross-examining party not within the subject matter of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I put our -- I put OTP's case to them, not our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I'm afraid I'll have to discuss it with my colleagues, and I'll do that. Apart from that, of course, although we have Rules on that, and we try to stick to the Rules, but it might be such a complex matter here that where rules of cross-examination do not strictly apply in this Court anyhow, that we try to take a cautious approach. But I'll first discuss it with my colleagues. We'll have a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, when further examining the witness, and I'm using this neutral term, not "re-examination," not "cross-examination," you're invited that to the extent there may be any doubt in the mind of the witness what the Prosecution's case is, that you inform him about that, not extensively and not the whole of the Prosecution case, but at least to the extent relevant for the questions you want to put to him. So to that extent, you're more or less in a situation where you are cross-examining the witness. At the same time, the Chamber does not encourage you in leading the witness the whole way down to his answer. You understand what I mean, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Kehoe, if there's at any point any further, without perhaps lengthy speeches, I think all parties and the Chamber know by now what -- where we are, more or less, trying to go between the Scylla and the Charybdis, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand Scylla and Charybdis is always a torturous path. Obviously, we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes you have to go and find your way through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And sometimes you hope for calm waters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We do preserve our record, noting our objections and methodology, but I know you understand that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, to the extent that you might have problems in understanding and if you are considering what position to take, I may remind you that Rule 89(A), last half sentence, is: " ... and shall not be bound by national rules of evidence." So some latitude there is to apply the Rules of Evidence and the spirit of the Statute and of the Rules. My last words, just not to be misunderstood, was "in the spirit of the Statute and the Rules."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, Mr. Russo will further examine you. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could please have Exhibit D1426.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you will recall during your cross-examination by Mr. Kehoe, he showed you this document from the 112th Brigade in OG Zadar, and he pointed out to you the fact that the artillery tasks for this unit did not include shelling the towns of Benkovac, Obrovac, or Gracac. What I wanted to know is, first of all, was the responsibility to fire artillery into the populated towns of Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac, was that the responsibility of the 112th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I object to the form of the question. In saying "the populated areas," there is no evidence of that. If he wants to say shooting into towns or firing into towns based on that order, that's fine, but anywhere populated is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you say "towns," of course, we later could ask whether the witness has any information about -- Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine. Your Honour, the focus of my question is whether or not the 112th Brigade had orders to fire into the towns of Benkovac, Obrovac, or Gracac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And was the -- well, given they didn't have orders to fire into those towns, would you expect the language which you issued -- the order which you issued to the corps artillery, that is, to shell the towns of Drvar, Knin, Obrovac and Benkovac, would you expect that that language would find its way into the orders of the 112th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the corps-level artillery?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, I mean the 112th Brigade. Would you expect your specific order, to shell the towns of Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac, would you expect that specific order to find its way into the orders for the 112th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about General Gotovina's offensive operation order, and you were asked if you had drafted a portion of that. You mentioned that there was a first version and then a second version of that order; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to show you an order by General Gotovina. Mr. President, this is -- just advising the Court, this is not on the 65 ter list. However, it does arise on re-direct. It is 65 ter 7144, and for the Court's information the OTP only received this document on, I believe, the 20th of January of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These are the same objections as previously raised, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The situation is slightly different, to the extent that I do understand that Mr. Russo says that the matter was introduced in cross-examination, that's one; and, second, so therefore to that extent he would be under an obligation to give you the list at the end of the cross-examination. And then he received it only recently, so there are slight differences to the usual situation. Anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Even on that score, he says he got it on the 20th of January --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That would be the 29th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says on the record on page 41, line 14, the 20th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, let's try to keep matters clear. I understood you to say that you received it on the 20th of January, and when Mr. Kehoe asked you when it was disclosed, that you answered the 29th of January. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, I understand. But if, in fact, it goes back to our original 92 ter, why in fact -- if counsel had anticipated to use this, why a motion wasn't made to put it on the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood that it was not raised by the 92 ter, but it was raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's my position, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not know yet what the document is, so it's a bit of guessing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is still part of the exhibit list that they had that they provided prior, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It was on the list of potential exhibits to use. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have considered to use it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may put the document to the witness, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have, Mr. Registrar, please, I'm sorry, 65 ter number 7144.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: While this is coming up, Mr. Rajcic, I will tell you this is an order by General Gotovina. It is dated the 1st of August. If we could turn to B/C/S page 13, English page 16, this would be section A -- 6A, I'm sorry, of the order, and there is -- this is an order that appears to mirror somewhat the offensive operation order. And I'd like to know, first of all, if you're aware of this order, and if you can explain to us what the distinctions are. Now, looking towards the middle of section 6A, you'll see it indicates: "Pursue the enemy in a planned fashion, while keeping the towns of Knin, Kistanje, Benkovac, Gracac, and Drvar under constant artillery fire." First, Mr. Rajcic, can you explain to us what this document is, where it fits in? In the planning of Operation Storm, was this one of the earlier drafts? Can you explain at all the distinction we find here?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first version. We can see the difference right away. The artillery group, if we're talking about the same document that we have in front of us, so the TS-2, the command post S, the village of Pokrovnik [phoen], firing position of the 130 guns, firing position of the Howitzer platoon is in the village of Kljuc. And in our work so far, when the two of us were on the same wavelength, you asked me how come that the Artillery Group 2 was also marked "TS-4" in my explanation, but if you compare the TS-2 in the second version of the 2nd of August, you will see that it is, in fact, TS-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for making that clarification, Mr. Rajcic. Now, the language that I read, the pursuing the enemy while keeping towns under constant artillery fire, can you explain why that language was changed from what we read here to what we read in the operative offensive operation order?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are talking about the pursuit of the enemy, what it means is it refers to certain combat activities that, in the course of an engagement, result in the formation of special pursuit groups. And then when a subsequent analysis is done or was done, we concluded that possibly it would not be possible to establish such pursuit groups because it is a specific combat activity that is carried out in the course of carrying out combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the language which indicates to keep the towns of Knin, Kistanje, Benkovac, Gracac, and Drvar under constant artillery fire, I understand that the towns themselves, in fact, changed, but does this expression of keeping the towns under constant artillery fire -- in your mind, is this the same interpretation that should be given to the final order, which was putting the towns under artillery fire? Do you see those as the same?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is supposed to mean that the targets in those towns were to be under constant artillery fire. It is a legitimate combat activity. In accordance with the Eastern Doctrine, it is called harassing fire and disruptive fire on enemy combat elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would offer 65 ter 7144.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's the same objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber allows the document admitted into evidence, which, of course, includes 65 ter problems resolved, and, Mr. Registrar, a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, you were also asked by Mr. Kehoe -- well, he put to you that the position of the OTP was that the Croatian forces fired the 122-millimetre multiple-barrel rocket-launcher systems into residential areas of Knin. You indicated that that was not the case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 122-millimetre?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, in answer to a question, that they were not targeting civilian facilities, but military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, you recall the discussion concerning the quarters of Mr. Martic [Realtime transcript read in error, "Markac"]. Do you recall that, during my examination?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And we were discussing where, if you can recall, that was located, and I believe on the target list it is indicated as a residential apartment complex; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you understand that to mean or did that mean that it was in a residential area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is only logical, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could you assist me in again the number -- the exhibit number on which the description appears?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that is on Exhibits P1271 and P1272.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry, I think there's an error in persona in interpretation, page 45, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's transcribed as "Mr. Markac," where you said "Mr. Martic."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be clear to everyone. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, I do recall, during that discussion, Mr. Rajcic, that you were -- you made it a point to emphasise to me that it was only the 130-millimetre cannon that was used to fire at the quarters of Mr. Martic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And as far as you are concerned, would there have been any problem, from your perspective, with firing the 122-millimetre multi-barrel rocket-launcher system at Mr. Martic's residential complex?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because of the rule of distinction, the obvious difference when we're talking about launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you perhaps explain a little bit more for the Chamber why that is a concern with the rocket-launcher system as opposed to not being a concern with the 130-millimetre cannon?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one analyses the use of multiple-barrel rocket-launchers, which has a greater density of projectiles, in terms of their impact on the target point, it covers a broader area with these rockets if you compare it with the 130-millimetre cannon, and the assessment was that the proportionality or the balance between what might happen to the buildings around the target was unacceptable. Therefore, it was unacceptable to fire on such a point, target, with the multiple rocket-launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, the reason I asked for the source is because you did not quote the language used in - what was it - P -- it's still MFI'd. It reads: "Apartment building complex." You added "residential," and in your question you emphasised the word "residential," which is not a correct reflection of what I find in the translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President. I do realise, now that the Court mentions it, that I had in my mind the regular reports of Captain Bruno Milan from the TS-4 that was firing on that target. I believe in his reports, he refers to it as a residential area. I don't have the exact exhibit number for that. However, I can provide it to the Court in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least in the list, it appears under a different name. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, to be clear --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Residential area or quarter is much bigger than a residential building. We will agree on that, won't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I certainly agree on that. Now, Mr. Rajcic, to be clear, the -- as far as you're aware, the 122-millimetre rocket systems were used to fire on the Slavko Rodic Barracks as well as the headquarters of the Main Staff in down-town Knin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and a roundabout intersection in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to turn, if we could, to your 92 ter statement, that is, Exhibit D1425. I'm looking specifically for paragraph 9. Now, in paragraph 9, Mr. Rajcic, you say: "I recall that at this meeting, General Gotovina emphasised that the goal was to obtain a military victory and that the operation was aimed only against enemy soldiers and nothing else ..." Now, that's not entirely true, is it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you're trying to target Mile Martic, but he's a political leader and the supreme commander of the forces, by virtue of his post, which means that he's a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that. However, what I'm putting to you is the fact that the operation itself was not simply aimed at a military victory over the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina, but in fact one of the objectives of this campaign, and in particular the artillery campaign, was, in fact, to get the civilians out so that the military would follow them; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit P461.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, you were present, were you not, at the presidential meeting in Brioni on 31 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And at that meeting, your supreme commander, President Tudjman, made clear to yourself, as well as to General Gotovina and others who were in attendance, that he believed the political situation to be so favourable that Croatia had an opportunity to not simply gain a military victory, but to remove the Serbian population from that area, and also at the same time to pay back the leaders of the RSK for attacks which they had perpetrated against Croatian towns and villages in the past; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could please move to B/C/S page 18, and English page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, what you're looking on your screen here, Mr. Rajcic, is a transcript of the Brioni meeting, and I'd like to go over a few of those portions with you. We can see here President Tudjman says: "Gentlemen, I accept your views in principle. There is something still missing, and that is the fact that in such a situation when we undertake a general offensive in the entire area, even greater panic will break out in Knin than has to date. Accordingly, we should provide for certain forces which will be directly engaged in the direction of Knin. And, particularly, gentlemen, please remember how many Croatian villages and towns have been destroyed, but that's still not the situation in Knin today ... Therefore, we will have to resolve this with UNCRO, this matter as well, and so forth. But their counter-attack from Knin and so forth, it would provide very good justification for this action and accordingly we have the pretext to strike, if we can, with artillery, you can ... for complete demoralisation ... not just this ..." Now, President Tudjman is saying a number of things in this passage. First of all, he's reminding everyone present, is he not, of the destruction wrought on Croatian towns and villages in the RSK, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Russo, this body of text that we see does not correspond, neither in its format, nor in its content, to -- with the meeting I attended on the 31st of July at Brioni. If you wish our communication to continue along these lines, then I would have to read the whole text, but I believe I can say with full responsibility that this piece of text I've read does not correspond, neither in terms of format, nor in terms of content, with the meeting I attended and the way developed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand your position with respect to that, Mr. Rajcic. Let me ask you: Do you deny that President Tudjman reminded everyone of the destruction in Croatian villages and towns?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting on the 31st of July, as I said, this is something I cannot recall hearing in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you deny that President Tudjman indicated that a counter-attack from Knin would provide very good justification for an artillery attack?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that on the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to look -- if we go to the next page in B/C/S and a bit further down the page in English, I'd like to look at a part of General Gotovina's response. He indicates: "Mr. President, at this moment we completely control Knin with our hardware. That's not a problem. If there is an order to strike at Knin, we will destroy it in its entirety in a few hours." Do you deny that General Gotovina told the supreme commander that if he were given an order, he could destroy Knin in its entirety in a few hours?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 31st of July, General Gotovina did not utter these words at Brioni.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I want to look a bit further into that paragraph at what else General Gotovina is proposing. He indicates: "The forces heading towards Knin are 400 good infantrymen from the 3rd Battalion, the 126th Regiment, who are all from this area, and they know the area through and through. They have reason to fight here, and at this moment it is difficult to keep them on a leash. There is the 1st Croatian 'zdrug,' which has 300 infantrymen, which has proved itself in this area at this moment, and in any case we can count on those infantrymen. There are special units of the Croatian and Herceg-Bosna MUP which have 350 excellent infantrymen, who have shown themselves to be outstanding in the operation. That means we have somewhere around 1.000 good infantrymen trained for assault operations, for quick transfers on this difficult terrain; we can easily take Knin, without any problem." Now, Mr. Rajcic, first of all, do you deny that General Gotovina told the supreme commander that he could easily take Knin with these thousand men?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as regards the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you aware of General Gotovina having told anyone, whether on the 31st of July or at another time, that Knin could be easily taken with these or any other men?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day when we were together, we did not part; and during that time he didn't say that to anyone on any occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Could you have, in fact, taken the town of Knin with troops and without artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my personal opinion that the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let's continue on, if we can. It's at the bottom of the page in English, from where President Tudjman begins: "Generals, officers ..." He states: "Generals, officers, although we must not do anything in an ill-conceived manner, we must proceed from the fact --"

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't have that on the screen. Now it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies. I will begin again: "Generals, officers, although we must not do anything in an ill-conceived manner, we must proceed from the fact that we have achieved such successes, from Western Slavonia and now in Bosnia, that we have gained the trust of the people, that we have the goodwill of the army --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. If we could just change the page on the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies. Continuing on: " ... the support of a good part of international public opinion, while the enemy is utterly demoralised. Therefore, we need to be bold. That means not just having things under control, but taking it as quickly as possible, so he gets a taste of it, and we pay him back. Therefore, no risky ventures like suffering losses to achieve success. Nevertheless, I think that the political situation is so favourable that we should focus on entering Knin as soon as possible."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, do you deny that President Tudjman said that at the 31July meeting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, in this context and in this sequence of sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Rajcic, it's true, isn't it, that President Tudjman was indicating to General Gotovina it was not simply enough to take Knin quickly, but that Knin itself had to get a taste of it, you had to pay back the RSK for what they'd done to other Croatian towns and villages; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When President Tudjman told General Gotovina that he did not want any risky ventures like suffering losses to achieve success, he was telling him, wasn't he, not to use troops, but rather to use artillery so as not to sacrifice any of the men and, therefore, not to have any troop losses in gaining that town; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now go to page 7. This is B/C/S page 12, and then it moves to 13. Looking specifically at the English in the middle of the top paragraph portion, where it begins: "It's all very well that the admiral ...," I believe that's the third sentence in on the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you find that portion on the B/C/S, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The penultimate sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, it states -- President Tudjman says: "It's all very well that the admiral is now supposed to close off their remaining three exits, but you are not providing them with an exit anywhere. There is no way out to ... ( ... to close it off). To pull out and flee; instead, you are forcing them to fight to the bitter end, which exacts a greater engagement and greater --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies. " ... which exacts a greater engagement and greater losses on our side. Therefore, let us also please take this into consideration because it's true, they are absolutely demoralised, and just as they have started moving out of Grahovo and Glamoc, when we put pressure on them, now they are already partly moving out of Knin. Accordingly, let us take into consideration, on a military level, the possibility of leaving them a way out somewhere, so they can pull out part of their forces ..." Now, President Tudjman is not simply indicating leaving the military a way out; he is, in fact, indicating to everyone, wasn't he, that the civilians should be left with a way out as well?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This manner of communication by President Tudjman with the commanders at the Brioni meeting on the 31st of July is something that did not take place. Both you and I could argue here about what was or was not said. When we're talking about this portion, there are only certain words that I recall as being said on the 31st of July, when I attended the meeting. Everything else did not take place. That's why I said that this transcript, in its form and content, does not tally with what took place on the 31st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you deny that President Tudjman indicated that people started leaving Grahovo and Glamoc when pressure was put on them? Do you deny that he said that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I deny it regarding that day when I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did President Tudjman ever indicate at any other time, in your presence, that people left Grahovo and Glamoc as a result of pressure being put on them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once, in a given situation in a given context, it was stated that there were civilians leaving Knin without any mention being made of pressure, direction, whether ways out should be left or not, about Admiral Domazet, who was not an officer but an intelligence person, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, when President Tudjman indicated -- well, first of all, let me ask you: The term or the phrase "putting pressure on someone," that is a phrase that is meant to convey the use of artillery to influence someone's decision-making; isn't that right? That's how you put pressure on someone?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that is the enemy army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when President Tudjman indicated "when we put pressure on them, now they are already partly moving out of Knin," now, it wasn't the Army of the RSK that was partly moving out of Knin on the 31st of July, was it; it was the civilians, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, do not keep referring me back to civilians and striking at civilians. That is something I did not hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, the question was a different one. The question was whether - and perhaps you focus on the last part - that on the 31st of July, whether civilians or non-civilians were leaving Knin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for the 31st of July and the meeting at Brioni, I remember it being said that only in the initial remarks by the president, that there was information to the extent that after the Croatian forces broke out at Dinara, the civilians began leaving Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think as a matter of fact that Mr. Russo was, in fact, referring to what he read from a transcript, whether right or wrong, which refers to ... they already partly moving out of Knin, and the question that was put to you by Mr. Russo was simply whether they partly leaving out of Knin, whether that could relate to the military or whether it was the civilian, if anyone at all, to leave Knin by that date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way I understood it was that civilians were leaving, not soldiers, that civilians were departing and not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic. If we could go now to B/C/S page 28, English page 15. I'm looking at the English in the third paragraph towards the middle, where it begins: "But I've said, and we've said it here ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you find that in the B/C/S, Mr. Rajcic? It is the words of the president.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood properly, it is the third sentence, beginning with: "Given the fact that I said it and that we said it ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, that's where I'm reading from: "But I've said, and we've said it here, that they should be given a way out here ... Because it is important that those civilians set out, and then the army will follow them, and when the columns set out, they will have a psychological impact on each other." Now, Mr. Rajcic, do you deny that President Tudjman told yourself, General Gotovina, and everyone present that it was important that the civilians set out?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could follow on to General Gotovina's response, and he states: "A large number of civilians are already evacuating Knin and heading towards Banja Luka and Belgrade. That means that if we continue this pressure, probably for some time to come, there won't be so many civilians, just those who have to stay, who have no possibility of leaving." Now, Mr. Rajcic, do you deny that General Gotovina told his supreme commander that by continuing the pressure and by "pressure" meaning artillery, that there wouldn't be so many civilians left?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I deny that. He never said this on the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did General Gotovina at any other time indicate that by putting pressure on civilians, that they would leave the area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the moment I was assigned to General Gotovina to be his first artillery man, I've never heard him say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to move to page 43 of the B/C/S, and it will move over to 44, but it's page 23 of the English. I'm looking at the part where Dr. Miroslav Tudjman -- where he begins saying: "Should the information be relayed ..." Dr. Miroslav Tudjman: "Should the information be relayed over the radio as to which routes are open for them to use to pull out?" And the president: "Yes, that should be said, not the fact that the routes are open, but that it has been noticed that civilians are getting out by using such and such a route." Dr. Miroslav Tudjman: "Can we say this at some point at the beginning of the operation? Can we publicise the fact so they know that the civilians are using these routes to withdraw?" The president responds: "Yes, it should be said that they have set out with passenger cars, and so on." Dr. Miroslav Tudjman: "But you will close off certain routes, and tell them which direction to head in, so we have as little to do as possible." Now, Mr. Rajcic, Dr. Miroslav Tudjman and President Tudjman here are discussing a way of informing the Serbian civilian population how to get out of the area so that the Croatian forces have less to do in forcing them out of that area; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, but I did not hear that on the 31st of July. I understand what is written here, but this is not what was said in this manner. There was no communication of this kind on the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, are you aware that General Gotovina did not object to the admission of this transcript, nor to the audio portion of this 31 July meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may. This was presented by the Office of the Prosecutor as something that was received by the Republic of Croatia. It came with an expert report basically saying, We don't know, given the technology, if this has been altered with or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, could we ask the witness to remove his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rajcic, could you please take off your headphones. Mr. Russo, how important is the knowledge of whether or not this is contested material for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It may be of some importance, Your Honour, if the witness honestly believes he needs to deny this in order to assist the accused. If he believes that the accused has no problem with it, that may not be an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether the accused has no problem with it, but it has not been, from what I understand, a strongly contested issue at this moment, whether this is original material, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, I took the information that came in good faith from the Office of the Prosecutor with that sheet on that piece of paper has the participants. I will note, and I'm sure that Mr. Russo will agree, that it does not have this witness as a participant in that meeting. Now, do I know what that means? Do I know if that's a speaker or people who attended, I'm not certain. I just know what we got and what I saw, and I can tell you that Marko Rajcic is not on that cover sheet. I stand to be corrected, but I believe that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, is there any chance that Mr. Rajcic attended another meeting on that same date in the same place? I mean, I'm addressing you, but I'm as much addressing the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I certainly don't know. I think the witness is saying he had gone to a meeting in Brioni, and it was on the 31st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is there any indication? I mean, would it make any sense if the Chamber would ask the parties to present any other material or any evidence they would have on the existence of a second meeting where -- that's what I understand from this witness, where the president and Mr. Gotovina and then this witness would have been present, apart from the one of which we have a transcript in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I recall the witness's testimony earlier, he noted that he was with General Gotovina all day on the 31st. I may be mistaken, but I think that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can ask him whether there was any other meeting at which the president was -- but whether there had been -- let's ask the witness to put his earphones on. Mr. Rajcic, take your time for a glass of water. Mr. Rajcic, on the 31st of July, when you were in Brioni, you told us what you remember from the meeting where the president, Mr. Tudjman, was attending and where Mr. Gotovina was attending as well. Now, was there another meeting during that day in which you and Mr. Gotovina and the president were attending, so were there two meetings with the three of you being present or was there one meeting with the three of you being present?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think he was -- if I may just interrupt. I think he was saying -- as drawing a difference between two meetings, one where he was present and one he was not. I think you put him at both.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the interpretation was not correct. If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So my question is -- perhaps I'll repeat it in order to avoid whatever confusion. Did you attend, on that 31st of July in Brioni, one meeting or more meetings where you, Mr. Gotovina and Mr. Tudjman were present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of Mr. Gotovina attending any other meeting than the one you remember where Mr. Tudjman also was present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
